chapters.title: Chapter 51. The Next Day After The Almost Threesome
paragraphs: The thin curtains in the inn room let in the morning sun, which made soft golden lines on the bed where Rex was sleeping between two women.

Mara’s grayish hair fell across the pillow on his left, and her face was calm in a way he had never seen when Garrett was around. And there’s Lily... curled up a little to his right, her breathing soft and steady, with one hand resting near his chest.
Rex slowly opened his eyes and let the feeling of satisfaction sink in. He needed last night to be just like that.

At first, the three of them were having an awkward conversation. Lily was shaking, and Mara looked defensive. However, he guided the conversation with a deft touch, adeptly manipulating their emotions.
Lily was crying tears of relief instead of shame by the end, and Mara had pulled the younger woman into an embrace that sealed their strange alliance.
What happened next was unavoidable.

"Last night was good shit as always... and today’s night is going to be... eh... average probably, knowing that I’m going to break her virginity." Rex thought to himself while looking at Lily’s sleeping face.
"Well... enough about that. I’m curious what will happen to my desire energy now that I did something different last night."
He moved a little, being careful not to wake either of them, and focused on the system interface that was behind his thoughts.
[DESIRE AUTHORITY SYSTEM - ENERGY UPDATE]
The familiar text scrolled across his mind’s eye, and Rex felt a spark of genuine excitement.
[ENERGY GENERATED: MARA KESSON]
[BASE GENERATION: 150 POINTS]
[SPECIAL BONUS APPLIED: SHARED EXPERIENCE WITH SECONDARY TARGET]
[MULTIPLIER: x2]
[TOTAL ENERGY GAINED: 300 POINTS]
[CURRENT TOTAL ENERGY: 650/800 FOR NEXT ABILITY UNLOCK]
Rex had to hold back a smile. "Ohh... it is different. That’s good."
Three hundred points in one night. The system had given him a reward for the threesome dynamic, which doubled Mara’s normal output because Lily was there.
From the perspective of a villain system, it made perfect sense. All of these things—corruption, manipulation, and breaking rules—were part of the main idea of desire as power.

He was only 150 points away from getting Foresight, a skill that would let him see possible futures and talk to people with almost perfect accuracy. And it’s even better to be in a fight with someone because he can predict their moves.
He had one more session with Mara, or he could push Lily to her limit and earn that first-time bonus. He was close either way.
[LILY VON STARLIGHT: 96/100]
[STATUS: POST-INTIMACY VULNERABILITY, EMOTIONAL DEPENDENCY MAXIMUM]
The number had gone up three points in one night. She was four points away from the highest score, and Rex knew exactly how to get there.
He just needs to give her time, love, and the reassurance that she is the only one who has him; even though she is sharing him with Mara, Rex can still make her feel like she is his one and only.
Let her know she’s special.
It was almost too simple.
Mara was the first to move next to him. Her eyes slowly opened and were unfocused for a moment before they found his face.
The smile on her face showed that she was thrilled, like someone who had stopped fighting for what they wanted.
"Morning," she said softly, her voice still rough from sleep.
"Morning," Rex said in a low voice so Lily wouldn’t wake up yet.
Mara moved in closer and kissed him softly on the shoulder. "Last night was great as always..."
"It was," he said, and he meant it.
He meant it, not in the way she probably assumed, but in a strategic way. Things had gone as planned.
Lily started to move on the other side of him. Her eyes opened, and for a moment she looked confused before she remembered what had happened.
Her cheeks turned pink right away, but instead of pulling away, she got closer and buried her face in his chest.
Lily said, "I-I... can’t believe that really happened," but her voice was muffled.
Rex put his arm around her and traced random patterns on her back with his fingers. "No regrets, right?"
She shook her head quickly. "No... none."
"I just... I never thought..." She stopped talking and couldn’t finish her sentence.
Mara reached over Rex to brush a strand of hair from Lily’s face. The gesture was surprisingly motherly given the situation.
"Sweetheart, it’s okay to feel overwhelmed. We’re all new to this."
Lily raised her head a little to look at Mara and then at Rex. "Are we... is this really okay?"
Rex gently cupped her cheek and made sure she was looking right into his eyes. "Lily, you’re important to me, and Mara’s also important to me."
"What we have doesn’t have to look like what other people have... as long as we’re honest with each other, that’s what matters."
The words were thoughtful and resonated deeply. Lily’s face changed from relief to love, and Mara’s hand found his and squeezed it gently.
[LILY VON STARLIGHT: 98/100]
Two points left.
"Come on," Rex said as he sat up slowly. "Let’s get breakfast going.
"I’m starving because of last night letting it all out... and I’m pretty sure the world hasn’t stopped turning just because we had a great night."
Both women laughed softly at that, and the tension that had been in the air for a while went away like morning mist.
Rex helped Mara make breakfast in the Broken Wheel Inn’s warm and familiar kitchen. The smell of rising bread and smoked meat filled the air.
Lily was still upstairs to wash up and change, so the two of them were alone for a while.

Mara worked quietly next to him, cracking eggs into a bowl while he cut bread from the loaf he had made the day before. It was easy to get into a rhythm with it, like the kind of partnership that comes from being close to each other a lot.
After a while, Mara said in a low voice, "You’re good with her."
Rex looked at her. "With Lily?"
"Mm~! She needed someone like you, someone who sees her."
He didn’t answer right away; instead, he focused on the bread. Mara wasn’t wrong, but she was also putting her own thoughts into the situation.
She needed someone to see her too, which is why she was in the kitchen with him instead of pretending to be a faithful wife.
Footsteps on the stairs interrupted them before they could say anything else. Rex looked up and saw Evelyn coming down into the common room.
Her face was blank, but her eyes were as sharp as ever. She wore plain clothes for traveling and had her dark purple hair pulled back in a useful braid.
"Morning," she said in a friendly way.
"Good morning, Evelyn," Rex said without hesitation. "You’re up early."
"I couldn’t sleep much," she said as she walked toward the kitchen. "I’m still thinking about everything that happened the other day."
Rex saw his chance and took it. "That makes two of us. I keep replaying that fight in my head."
Evelyn’s face changed a little, and something that was hiding fell away. "You took a hit that should have killed you... that axe was meant for Elliot."
"Maybe that’s what I call a reflex," Rex said with a shrug and put down the knife. "I didn’t really think about it."
"That’s what makes it so great." Evelyn crossed her arms and leaned against the doorframe. "Most people freeze when they get that close to death. You moved toward it."
[EVELYN ASTRALIGHT: 15/100 → 18/100]
[OBSERVATION: REASSESSING INITIAL JUDGMENT, RESPECT BUILDING]
"I’ve been thinking about what you said," Rex said, moving a little closer so that their conversation seemed more private.
Mara was still there, but she had started humming and paying attention to the eggs. "About being careful and also not trusting everyone."
Evelyn’s eyes got a little smaller, but they were also curious. "And?"

chapters.title: Chapter 52. Let’s Try a Bow! (I’ll Try to Shot Her Heart First)
paragraphs: Rex locked the fuck in when he was about to say something that could have given him the chance to be closer to her.
"You were right to be suspicious of me when I first showed up." Rex giggled while rubbing the back of his head. If I were you, I’d do the same thing to protect someone I cared about."
He stopped for a moment to let that sink in. "But I hope you know my heart is in the right place after all this."
She looked at him for a long time, and Rex could almost see the numbers running through her mind.

She was a reincarnator with a system of some kind, probably one that made her better at seeing things or fighting, since she killed the Goblin King with one blow. She was trying to figure him out and find the angle, but all she saw was sincerity because he was giving it to her.
Or at least a very good copy of it.
"I think you’re genuine," Evelyn said finally. "And I think Elliot is lucky to have you looking out for him."
Rex lied smoothly, "He’s a good guy, and he deserves people who will be there for him."
Evelyn’s face relaxed a little bit. "Yes, he does..."
"Thank you, Rex."
[EVELYN ASTRALIGHT: 18/100 → 21/100]
[OBSERVATION: TRUST BUILDING, DEFENSIVE BARRIERS LOWERING]
"Anytime," Rex said, and he meant it in the most selfish way possible.
At that moment, Mara said that breakfast was ready, and the rest of the family began to come down.
Elliot came in with his usual loud energy, followed by Helena with a book under her arm. Diana came down last, already dressed for possible training even though nothing was officially planned.
Lily came out of her room looking fresh and beautiful. Her eyes immediately found Rex’s across the room.
She smiled at him in a way that was just for him, and he nodded back in a way that was not... obvious.
The group sat down at the long table, and breakfast became a relaxed event with lots of easy conversation. Rex sat between Helena and Diana, as he always does, in a smart way.
Evelyn was sitting next to Elliot on the other side of him, and Lily was sitting at the end of the table next to Mara.
Rex turned his attention to Diana when the conversation slowed down.
He asked, "So for today’s training? What kind of training are we going to have?" in a casual way.
Diana shook her head and cut into her eggs. "There’s no training for today."
"We’re giving everyone a day off after the Goblin King incident, but I might practice by myself this afternoon."
"Archery?"
"Always archery," she said with a small smile. "It’s what I’m best at."
Rex had noticed that Diana was very proud of her skills in their past talks. It was one of the things that made her who she was and gave her value in a group where Elliot got most of the attention.
He had never seen a better archer than her, and she knew it.
"I’d love to watch if you don’t mind," Rex said. "That’s always been something I’ve been interested in."
Diana’s face lit up a lot. "Really? Most people think it’s about letting go and pulling back."
"Then people are idiots for having a trash opinion," Rex said, making her laugh for real. "Hahahahaha~! You really are someone who’s easily curious about anything, huh?"
[DIANA VON STARLIGHT: 25/100 → 28/100]
[OBSERVATION: PRIDE ENGAGED, RECEPTIVE TO ATTENTION]
Diana said, "Come to the practice field after lunch then, if you’re still interested after that hour, of course."
"I’ll show you some good exercises that can be used for your future." Diana said while pointing at Rex with a wink.
"Okay." Rex thought to himself then. "Bingo... now I can try to be closer to Diana since she’s the second easiest target."

The sun was warm in the afternoon, but not too hot, which made it ideal weather for training outside. Rex walked to the practice field behind the inn, where Diana was already there with her bow and a target about fifty meters away.
She looked over at him as he got closer and gave him a quick nod. "Just in time."
"And I’m surprised you’re still interested."
"Wouldn’t miss it," Rex said, stopping a respectful distance away so he wouldn’t bother her.

Diana nocked an arrow with ease, pulled back the string until it touched the corner of her mouth, and let go. The arrow flew straight and true, hitting the center ring of the target with a satisfying thunk.
Rex said, "That’s impressive," and he meant it.
There was nothing wrong with her form... she legitimately looked like an expert at it.
"That’s just child’s play for me," Diana said as she nocked another arrow. "Look at the real one like this."
She quickly drew and shot three arrows, each one landing within a few inches of the first. The speed and accuracy were truly amazing, thanks to years of hard work and practice.

Rex watched her do a few more drills, taking notes on her technique and how she changed her stance slightly for different distances and wind conditions. She was completely at ease, and he could feel the confidence coming from her.
After twenty minutes, she put down her bow and looked at him. "So, hotshot... wanna give it a quick shot to see if you have the potential to use one?"
Rex said, "I’ve never touched a bow before," which was true for this body.
"Then you should definitely try your first today," Diana said, pointing to her gear. "Come on."
"I’ll guide you through the process."
Rex came over and let her show him how to stand and hold the weapon correctly. She was calm and thorough, changing his posture without getting too involved.
When he finally pulled back the string and let go of his first arrow, it flew far off target and stuck in the grass, a few meters to the left of it.
Diana laughed, but not in a mean way. "Hahaha~! Not bad for a first try.
"Most people don’t even make it that far."
Rex said with a big sigh, "I’m really fucking bad at this."
"Come on now, don’t be down just because of that." Diana patted his back.
"You just need to practice." Diana took her bow back and showed him again. "Archery is all about consistency, muscle memory, and doing the same thing over and over."
"Don’t forget to use your brain to calculate everything too... an idiot would fail right away to try archery." Diana giggled. "No offense, though... I didn’t mean that statement for you."
Rex then had an idea that would make Diana feel positive about herself and give them a chance to talk again in the future. He waited until she had made another perfect shot before he spoke.
"How about we make it interesting?" he asked in a casual tone.
"Hm?" Diana raised an eyebrow. "Interesting, huh...? What do you mean by that?"
"A challenge! You and I against each other." Rex smirks. "If I can hit the target even once in five tries, I win."
"If I can’t, you win."
Diana said while holding a laugh, "Pfftt...! That’s not fair at all, you know?!"
"You just got started as an amateur."
"Exactly. That’s why I’m willing to bet on it," Rex said with a smile. "The loser has to do something embarrassing, and of course... the winner gets to choose how embarrassing it is."
He could tell when she became competitive, especially when her expression locked in right away. Diana was a charming person, but she also took her skills very seriously.
She was drawn to the idea of a challenge, even a lopsided one, because it spoke to something deep inside her.
"What kind of embarrassing?" she asked, both curious and suspicious.
"Nothing mean. Just something that would be a delightful story later."
Diana thought about it for a second and then shrugged. "Okay then, I accept that easily!"
"You have five arrows, and if even one hits the target, you win right away."
"Aight! Bet!" They shook hands, and Rex got back into position.
Diana gave him five arrows, and he pretended to nock the first one carefully, check his stance, and take his time aiming.
The arrow flew and missed by a considerable distance.
"Four left," Diana said, sounding like she was having fun.
"At this point you’re just going to make a fool out of yourself, hahaha~!"

"There’s not going to be a single man getting close to her other than me, but still...
I needed more girls to fuck." Rex said while trying not to laugh.
"Oh well..."
Rex could still feel the echo of her love, how she had given herself to him completely without thinking twice or feeling bad about it.
It was exactly what he needed, and the system didn’t take long to confirm it.
[ACHIEVEMENT COMPLETE: LILY VON STARLIGHT MAXIMUM DEVOTION]
[MAXIMUM DESIRE BONUS CLAIMED: 1000 DESIRE ENERGY]
[TOTAL ENERGY AVAILABLE: 1650 POINTS]
The notification came up right after it was over, and Rex felt a rush of happiness that had nothing to do with the act itself.
Rex had earned a thousand points, indicating that he had sufficient energy to activate his next powerful ability, in addition to the ones he already possessed.
"Fuck yeah!
Now that is what I’ve been waiting for." Rex clenched his right fist.
"It came just in time for the perfect plan of slowly destroying this town!"
He turned his attention inward and easily pulled up the system interface.
"System, let’s fucking do it now!
Unlock Full Potential Foresight." He said while snapping his fingers.
[ABILITY PURCHASE CONFIRMED]
[FORESIGHT (FULL POTENTIAL) - 800 POINTS]
[REMAINING ENERGY: 850 POINTS]
[ABILITY DETAILS: FORESIGHT ALLOWS USER TO PERCEIVE POTENTIAL FUTURES UP TO 60 SECONDS AHEAD.]
[CLARITY INCREASES WITH FOCUS.]
[MULTIPLE TIMELINE BRANCHES VISIBLE SIMULTANEOUSLY.]
[COMBAT APPLICATIONS: PREDICT ENEMY MOVEMENTS, AVOID FATAL STRIKES, IDENTIFY OPTIMAL ATTACK WINDOWS.]
Rex felt a change as soon as the ability became part of his mind.
Initially, the ability felt like a faint whisper on the periphery of his consciousness, but upon focusing, the world appeared to fragment into scattered images.
He could see himself lying in bed, but he could also see himself sitting up in three seconds or turning to check on Lily in five.
The timelines split and came back together, showing him what would happen right away if he did each of the things he was thinking about.
Rex thought, "This is fucking crazy," as he pushed the limits.
He saw his hand move before he actually moved it.
The prediction was spot on, even to the tiniest twitch of his fingers.
"If I’m able to utilize this, then I’m sure that, in the near future...
I could just fight my way in against everyone until I get everything I want!"
With Foresight on, fighting would be almost too easy.
He could see attacks coming before they even started, dodge blows that weren’t even thrown yet, and get ready for counterattacks with superhuman accuracy.
Along with his telekinesis, he was getting to be very dangerous.
"System, recommend me the next ability I should get to be even more overpowered." Rex asked in his head.
[NEXT RECOMMENDED ABILITY: INFINITE REGENERATION (FULL POTENTIAL)]
[COST: 3000 DESIRE ENERGY]
[ABILITY DETAILS: COMPLETE CELLULAR REGENERATION.
FATAL WOUNDS HEAL WITHIN SECONDS.
LIMB REGROWTH POSSIBLE.
IMMUNITY TO POISON, DISEASE, AND AGING EFFECTS.
STAMINA RECOVERY INSTANTANEOUS.]
Rex felt his eyebrows raise when he saw that the cost was three thousand points.
That was more than three times what Foresight had cost and almost four times what he had right now.

He would need to have a lot of maximum devotion targets or have a lot of sessions with the ones he already has to get that much, but still he can utilize the multiplier that comes from a threesome or maybe soon... a foursome.
"Noted," he muttered.
"But that’s a problem for future Rex."

"But still... it’s fucking expensive, but I ain’t going to complain because getting desire energy is easy, and soon I’ll need to be more creative to make a huge amount of desire energy every single day."
At least he had foresight for now, and that was all he needed.
He allowed the ability to relax into a passive state, which kept him aware of what was going to happen in the next few seconds without overwhelming his senses.
It was like having a sixth sense, a quiet warning system that would let him know when trouble was coming before it happened.
He turned his head to look at Lily, who was still sleeping soundly next to him.
She looked younger when she was sleeping, weak, and completely at peace.
A small part of him, the part that wasn’t completely focused on strategy, felt something like affection.
She had never doubted his motives and had given him everything she had.
Rex thought, "You really are too good for this world," as he reached out to brush a strand of hair from her face.
"And that’s why you’re perfect for me."
He lay back down on the pillow and closed his eyes for a moment.
The Foresight ability hummed at the edge of his mind, showing him bits and pieces of the near future.
For the next minute or so, nothing really interesting will happen.
It was a quiet morning, and Lily was still sleeping as the sun rose higher.
Then the vision changed.
Rex saw flames sixty seconds ahead.
There was also many screaming came from villagers and the sound of wood breaking.
He quickly opened his eyes and focused harder on the Foresight, pushing it to show him more details.
The ambush by the bandits.
It was happening now, just as he had told Kruger to do it three days ago.
"Ahh yes...
Perfect fucking timing," Rex thought with a grim sense of satisfaction.
"Right when everyone is still waking up and confused."
He sat up slowly so he wouldn’t wake Lily up.
There was no reason to scare her before it was necessary.
He quickly put on his clothes, moving with perfect accuracy because the Foresight showed him exactly where each piece of clothing was before he reached for it.
And then...
BAAAMMMMM!
The first explosion shook the village as he was finishing getting ready.
The sound was like thunder, a deep boom that shook the inn’s walls and sent dust flying from the ceiling beams.
Lily woke up right away, her eyes wide with fear and confusion.
"WHAT WAS THAT...?!" she gasped as she held the blanket to her chest.
"Stay here," Rex said in a calm but firm voice.
"After I leave, lock the door.
Only let me or your family in, okay?"
"R-Rex... what’s going on?" Lily looked concerned when she asked that.
But then a second explosion, this time closer.
The window shook in its frame, and a woman screamed outside.
BAAAMMMMM!
"Bandits," Rex said simply.
"They’re attacking the village."
Lily’s face turned white.
"We have to help!
We have to—"
"You need to stay safe," Rex said as he walked to the window.
"Your family will take care of the main force."
"I’ll make sure no one gets to the inn."
"And... can you even walk, though?" Rex asked with a smile on his face.
"I..." Lily felt a wave of embarrassment as she realized Rex was right.
It was because of yesterday’s intense session; she felt sore all over her body, and even her legs refused to respond to any command.
He didn’t give her a chance to argue.
He could see the next few seconds clearly because of his foresight.
But still...
Lily would try to get out of bed, realize she was still naked, and then rush to find her nightgown.
That would give him enough time to get out and look around.
"Don’t try anything reckless when I’m out." He gave another clear answer to her.
Rex opened the window and climbed out onto the narrow ledge.
Then, with his telekinesis, he pulled himself up onto the roof.
As soon as he got past the edge, he could see the whole attack.
There was a lot of chaos happening in the village.
Three different places had fires, and black smoke was rising into the sky in the morning.
There were many bandits in the streets, at least thirty or forty of them, all of them armed with swords, axes, and other crude weapons.
They were attacking without thinking, breaking windows, kicking down doors, and killing anyone who tried to fight back.
Rex’s improved vision found Kruger near the middle of the raid.
The huge bandit leader shouted orders and swung a war hammer that smashed a merchant’s stall with one blow.
His men were attacking in a coordinated way, which showed that they were following a plan and not just stealing things at random.
Rex thought, "Good."
"They’re doing exactly what I told them to do..."

chapters.title: Chapter 62. I Wish I Had Popcorn: A Villain’s Review of His Own Attack
paragraphs: Then his foresight kicked in and showed him what would happen in the next ten seconds. He saw Elliot come out of the inn’s main door, sword drawn and face twisted in righteous rage.
Behind him came Evelyn, moving with that supernatural speed that marked her as a reincarnator.
Diana stood on a roof across the square with a bow in her hand and an arrow already nocked.
Helena came out last, and her hands were already crackling with magical energy.
The hero group was getting ready to move.

Rex crouched low on the roof, staying hidden behind the chimney while still being able to see the battlefield below. His foresight was working extra hard now, showing him how the fight would go in different ways.
In most scenarios, the Starlight family would emerge victorious, but there would still be casualties among the villagers. In certain timelines, one of the villagers suffered serious injuries.
Elliot got too sure of himself in one very dark branch and ended up with a bandit’s axe in his ribs.
Rex felt a wave of nausea as he watched Elliot, as usual. "What a fucking loser... why is he always on the brink of death in every fight? Does he really need saving all the time?!"
"Can’t have that." Rex said, "Not yet, anyway."
He took a seat to observe, prepared to intervene should the situation spiral out of control.
"If only I had some popcorn on me... I’d be enjoying this."
Elliot ran out into the street, his sword shining in the morning light. The first bandit he saw barely had time to realize he was in danger before Elliot’s sword hit him in the chest.
The Heroic Strike skill made the blow strong enough to lift the man off his feet and send him crashing into a wall.
Elliot shouted, "EVERYONE...! Get inside!" His voice cut through the noise. "Block your doors and make sure to not let any stranger in!"
Three bandits turned towards him, their smiles befitting men who believed they had the advantage due to their numbers. They spread out, weapons raised, in an attempt to surround him.
Elliot didn’t wait for them to get ready. He charged the one on the left, swinging his sword in a wide arc that made the bandit have to block.

The sound of steel hitting steel echoed in the air, but Elliot was already turning, using his speed to spin past the first attacker and slash at the second. The bandit yelled and fell back, blood pouring from a cut on his shoulder.
The third bandit tried to take advantage of Elliot’s back, rushing in with an overhead chop. But a flash of silver flew through the air, and the man suddenly had an arrow sticking out of his thigh.
He fell down screaming, and Diana’s voice could be heard from the roof.
"Be more careful this time, Elliot!
"I had him!" Elliot shouted back, but his smile showed that he was grateful for the help.
Evelyn moved through the battlefield like a ghost, a blur of motion. Her sword was shorter than Elliot’s and made for speed instead of power.
She used it with the skill of a surgeon. She came up behind a bandit who was trying to set a bakery on fire, and her sword found the space between his ribs before he knew she was there.
She was gone before the body hit the ground and was already on her way to her next target.
Rex was very interested in what she was doing. Even with years of training, no normal person could move as fast as she did.
It had to be a system ability, something that made her body stronger than any other human’s. With her fighting instincts, she was cutting through the bandits like they were made of paper.
Helena stood in the middle of the square, using her body as a place for the villagers to gather as they ran away. She moved her hands in complicated patterns, casting spells with ease.
"Flame Lance!" she shouted, and three flaming spears appeared in the air around her.
With a wave, they all shot forward, hitting different targets. The bandits who were hit fell down screaming, and their clothes caught fire as they tried to put out the flames.
Two bandits tried to sneak up on her from the side, thinking that a mage would be weak up close. They quickly realized their mistake.
Helena’s hand shot out, and the ground under their feet suddenly froze. They fell hard, and before they could get up, sharp stone spikes shot up from the ground and stabbed them.
"Nice try, you lost pigs," Helena said calmly as she turned to look for her next target. "Stone Spikes..."
Diana was showing them why they thought she was the best archer they had ever seen. She gracefully traversed the rooftops, her bow resonating with each shot.
Every shot was perfect. An arrow went through the hand of a bandit trying to break into a house, making him drop his weapon with a scream.
Another person who was pursuing a woman as she fled received an arrow in the knee, causing him to crash face-first into the ground.
A third person who was trying to flank Elliot suddenly got an arrow in the shoulder, which spun him around and left him open for Elliot’s final blow.
Diana shouted, "Three more coming from your left!" and Elliot quickly moved to the side.
It was impressive how well they worked together. They had fought together so often that they knew where each other would be and what they needed.
It was the kind of teamwork that only comes after years of fighting together.

But the bandits weren’t going to give up easily. They had many people on their side, and even though each one of them couldn’t beat the hero party on their own, they were starting to work together to attack.

Five people rushed Elliot from different sides at the same time, forcing him to defend himself. His sword flashed in a complicated pattern, blocking and deflecting, but he was still being pushed back.
"Lightning Bolt!" Helena’s voice cut through the noise, and a crackling stream of electricity shot across the square, hitting one of Elliot’s attackers right in the chest.
The man shook and fell, and smoke rose from his burned armor.
That was the chance Elliot needed. He turned on his Heroic Strike again, and his sword started to glow with golden light.
He swung it in a wide, horizontal arc, and the energy wave that followed the blade hit two more bandits, sending them flying backward with broken ribs and broken weapons.
Evelyn now starts to move like an assassin behind the shadows. Her sword found the throat of another bandit before she disappeared back into the chaos.
The group that had tried to overpower Elliot was either dead or running away in a matter of seconds.
"FORM UP, YOU DAMN PIECES OF TRASH!" Kruger’s voice rang out over the battlefield. "Don’t try to spread out, you pussies!
"Try to use more group tactics like you always do!"
The bandits started to regroup, moving back into tighter groups. It was harder to pick them off one at a time, but area attacks were better against them.
Helena saw the chance right away. Her hands started to glow with a bright blue light, and the air around her got noticeably colder.
Ice crystals formed in the air and began to swirl in a bigger vortex. "It ends here..."
She shouted, "Ice Storm!" and the spell came to life.

A blizzard of razor-sharp ice shards shot out from Helena’s position, covering an area of at least twenty meters. The bandits who had banded together suddenly found themselves in a storm of freezing projectiles and cutting wind. A few fell right away, their bodies torn apart by the ice.
Others staggered back, bleeding from a lot of cuts, and their movements were slowed by the sudden cold.
Diana used the moment to great effect. She shot three arrows at once, which should have been impossible, but she made it look easy, and she did it quickly.
Each arrow hit a different target, and each target fell.
Elliot yelled, "How many are there left?!"
He was out of breath but still ready to fight for more.
"At least fifteen of those bandits are still standing!" Diana said as she looked around the battlefield.
"And they’re getting smarter!"

chapters.title: Chapter 63. I’ll Let Him Meet His Childhood Crush, and Surprise! Surprise! She’s Mine!
paragraphs: What Diana said was correct. The remaining bandits had stopped attacking and were starting to retreat toward the edge of the village, using buildings and other cover to shield themselves from Diana’s arrows and Helena’s magic.
Even in the middle of the chaos, it was easy to see Kruger because of how big he was. He was swinging that huge war hammer around like it was nothing, and his face was twisted with rage.
He shouted, "So... you’re one of the boys I heard about, eh?!"
Elliot starts to show his sword stances with a fierce look in his eyes. "Yeah, what about it...?"
"You want to be a hero...?" and pointed the hammer at Elliot. "Okay, boy...! Let’s see what you can do when facing a real threat!"
When Elliot heard that, he began to frown, and Rex could see that his pride had overridden his common sense.
Elliot didn’t wait for help or talk to his team for any planning other than just ran straight at Kruger, like a typical main character as always.
"Elliot, wait!" Helena shouted, but it was too late.
Kruger swung his hammer at Elliot, which should have crushed his head. Elliot managed to evade the hammer at the last moment, causing it to collide with the cobblestones where he had been standing.
He swung back at Kruger, aiming for his exposed side, but the bandit leader was faster than he looked. He turned away, and Elliot’s sword only made a small cut across his ribs.
"Hmph! Not bad for a naive kid like you!"
They start to hit each other a lot, with Elliot’s speed against Kruger’s raw strength. It was an impressive show, but Rex knew how it would end.

Kruger had more experience in battle, employed more dirty tricks, and was unafraid to fight to the death, whereas Elliot, despite being skilled, still exhibited a naive hero tendency to hold back and prioritize disabling strikes over lethal ones.
Evelyn also saw the issue. She tried to go around Kruger and hit him from the side, but three bandits stopped her and made her fight them instead.
Diana fired one arrow after another at Kruger, but the large man deflected them with his hammer. The arrows broke against the metal head.
She was able to get one past his guard and hit him in the shoulder, but he didn’t seem to notice. He pulled it out and kept fighting.
Helena was getting ready to cast another big spell, and her hands were moving in complicated ways, but it would take time. Elliot might not have that time.
From his perch on the roof, Rex saw all of these events happen. His foresight showed him the many possible paths that could lead to different outcomes.
Most of the time, Elliot survived, although with severe injuries. In some cases, Kruger was able to kill someone before anyone could stop him.
"Not yet," Rex said quietly. "I need him to stay alive for a little longer."
But before he could decide whether to get involved, his Foresight lit up with a new warning. A different timeline, in which the inn itself was attacked.
He focused his enhanced perception on the building below him.
There he saw... a single person moving purposefully through the chaos, heading straight for the Broken Wheel Inn.
He was shorter than most of the other bandits and wore a hooded cloak that hid his face. He had two daggers in his hands, and the way he moved made it clear that he had trained for serious combat.
Rex’s foresight told him what would happen. The figure would get to the inn, kick in the front door, and go straight to the private rooms.
Mara and Garrett were still there, and Lily was too.
And as the figure got closer, Rex finally saw his face clearly under the hood.
Marcus.
"What the fuck is he doing here...?"
Rex then realized what he had just planned three days ago. "Ain’t he supposed to lead the attack?!"
"Okay now... he’s fucked!" Rex clenched both his fists.

Rex fell off the roof and used his telekinesis to slow his fall and land quietly in the alley next to the inn. He hurried to the front door and got there just as Marcus kicked it open with a loud bang.
He could hear Garrett and Mara screaming inside. Rex pushed through the broken door and saw Marcus coming toward the couple, his daggers shining wickedly in the low light.
Garrett stood in front of Mara with a fishing knife that looked weak compared to Marcus’s weapons. His hands were shaking, but he didn’t give up.
"S-S-Stay back...!" Garrett yelled, his voice breaking. "I w-won’t let you hurt my wife!"
Rex recognized Garrett as a coward, which led him to believe that taking Mara for himself was the right choice all along.
A woman as beautiful as Mara deserved someone far better than this pathetic man who valued fishing over his wife’s safety.
"Hahahahahaha...!" Marcus laughed, but it was a cold sound that wasn’t funny. "A fisherman playing the hero, eh? This will be quick and easy."
He moved forward so quickly that Garrett couldn’t react. One dagger swept toward the older man’s throat.
Rex’s telekinesis stopped the blade in mid-swing, as if it had hit an invisible wall. Marcus’s eyes got bigger because he was confused, and then Rex came into view.
"Okay now... that’s far enough," Rex said in a calm voice. "And it seems like you went overboard with this stupid decision."
Marcus turned to him, and his face lit up with recognition, but then he started to pretend, as he was ordered to by Rex. "Whoa, hey! You’re the one who’s been at the hero party!"
"Yeah," Rex said, stepping in front of Marcus and the couple, knowing that Marcus still acted like he didn’t know him from three days ago.
"Garrett, take Mara to the root cellar and lock the door... Don’t come out until someone from the Starlight family comes to get you."
"But what about you?" Garrett stammered.
"Just get your ass to move now! I’ll be fine." Rex said while doing stretches.
Mara said. "Come on, Garrett! You heard him!"
Mara took her husband’s arm and pulled him to the back of the inn. They went through a door, and Rex heard a heavy bar slide into place.
Marcus watched them leave, then focused all of his attention on Rex. It was hard to tell what he was feeling because his face showed both anger and something else.
And it felt like something more personal.
"You know who I am," Rex said, and it wasn’t a question.
"I know you’re in the way," Marcus said, tightening his grip on his daggers. "Stop with all of this drama now because the boss knew your plan right away by using us all!"
Rex laughed. "I fucking knew it... and it seems like it was a dumb move to try and stab me in the back anyway.
Rex grinned. "I think we have more to talk about than you think..."
"Come with me. I want to show you something."

He turned and walked toward the stairs without looking back to see if Marcus was following. His foresight told him that curiosity would win out over caution, and sure enough, he heard Marcus’s footsteps behind him.
"What the fuck do you want to show to me...?"
They went up to the second floor, and Rex took him to the room where Lily was. He knocked once, letting her know that it’s him.
"Come in!" Lily answered right away, and then he opened the door.
Marcus’s body was already in shock hearing those familiar voices coming from the room, and when they enter the room... both of them can see Lily.
Lily was now dressed and sitting on the edge of the bed with her arms around her knees. When she saw Marcus, her eyes got bigger, and something complicated flashed across her face.
It was recognition, confusion, and a little bit of old pain.
"M-Marcus...?" she said in a quiet voice.
"N-No way..." Marcus stopped in the doorway, and his daggers dropped a little. "L-Lily? Is that r-really you..."
"Wait... now I remember... you’re one of them too... I fucking forgot!" Marcus said while hitting his head softly.
"What are you doing here...?" His eyes moved around the room, taking in the messy bed, Lily’s messy hair, and the close atmosphere. "W-What the fuck...?"
His face went from pale to red as he began to understand what had happened to Lily, and then he started to get angry. "Y-You...!"
Marcus’s voice, barely audible above a whisper, resembled a scream. "What the FUCK did you do to her!?"
"What did you accuse me of?" Rex asked.
"Don’t spill that shit on my face...! You... showing me this, I fucking knew that you are one sly motherfucker!" Marcus said while pointing at him.
Rex shut the door behind them, locking the three of them in the room. "Well... Marcus, I didn’t do anything she didn’t want."
Rex glanced at her. "Isn’t that right, Lily?"
Lily’s face turned red, but she nodded. "Yes... I wanted this... I wanted him."
Marcus looked like he had been hit in the stomach. "No...!"
"No, you don’t understand this situation at all, Lily...! You don’t know what you’re saying!"
"He’s controlling you, he’s—"
"I’m sorry, Marcus... but I already fell in love with him," Lily said, her voice getting stronger.
"I love Rex."

sentences.text: What Diana said was correct.
The remaining bandits had stopped attacking and were starting to retreat toward the edge of the village, using buildings and other cover to shield themselves from Diana’s arrows and Helena’s magic.
Even in the middle of the chaos, it was easy to see Kruger because of how big he was.
He was swinging that huge war hammer around like it was nothing, and his face was twisted with rage.
He shouted, "So... you’re one of the boys I heard about, eh?!"
Elliot starts to show his sword stances with a fierce look in his eyes.
"Yeah, what about it...?"
"You want to be a hero...?" and pointed the hammer at Elliot.
"Okay, boy...!
Let’s see what you can do when facing a real threat!"
When Elliot heard that, he began to frown, and Rex could see that his pride had overridden his common sense.
Elliot didn’t wait for help or talk to his team for any planning other than just ran straight at Kruger, like a typical main character as always.
"Elliot, wait!" Helena shouted, but it was too late.
Kruger swung his hammer at Elliot, which should have crushed his head.
Elliot managed to evade the hammer at the last moment, causing it to collide with the cobblestones where he had been standing.
He swung back at Kruger, aiming for his exposed side, but the bandit leader was faster than he looked.
He turned away, and Elliot’s sword only made a small cut across his ribs.
"Hmph!
Not bad for a naive kid like you!"
They start to hit each other a lot, with Elliot’s speed against Kruger’s raw strength.
It was an impressive show, but Rex knew how it would end.

Kruger had more experience in battle, employed more dirty tricks, and was unafraid to fight to the death, whereas Elliot, despite being skilled, still exhibited a naive hero tendency to hold back and prioritize disabling strikes over lethal ones.
Evelyn also saw the issue.
She tried to go around Kruger and hit him from the side, but three bandits stopped her and made her fight them instead.
Diana fired one arrow after another at Kruger, but the large man deflected them with his hammer.
The arrows broke against the metal head.
She was able to get one past his guard and hit him in the shoulder, but he didn’t seem to notice.
He pulled it out and kept fighting.
Helena was getting ready to cast another big spell, and her hands were moving in complicated ways, but it would take time.
Elliot might not have that time.
From his perch on the roof, Rex saw all of these events happen.
His foresight showed him the many possible paths that could lead to different outcomes.
Most of the time, Elliot survived, although with severe injuries.
In some cases, Kruger was able to kill someone before anyone could stop him.
"Not yet," Rex said quietly.
"I need him to stay alive for a little longer."
But before he could decide whether to get involved, his Foresight lit up with a new warning.
A different timeline, in which the inn itself was attacked.
He focused his enhanced perception on the building below him.
There he saw... a single person moving purposefully through the chaos, heading straight for the Broken Wheel Inn.
He was shorter than most of the other bandits and wore a hooded cloak that hid his face.
He had two daggers in his hands, and the way he moved made it clear that he had trained for serious combat.
Rex’s foresight told him what would happen.
The figure would get to the inn, kick in the front door, and go straight to the private rooms.
Mara and Garrett were still there, and Lily was too.
And as the figure got closer, Rex finally saw his face clearly under the hood.
Marcus.
"What the fuck is he doing here...?"
Rex then realized what he had just planned three days ago.
"Ain’t he supposed to lead the attack?!"
"Okay now... he’s fucked!" Rex clenched both his fists.
Rex fell off the roof and used his telekinesis to slow his fall and land quietly in the alley next to the inn.
He hurried to the front door and got there just as Marcus kicked it open with a loud bang.
He could hear Garrett and Mara screaming inside.
Rex pushed through the broken door and saw Marcus coming toward the couple, his daggers shining wickedly in the low light.
Garrett stood in front of Mara with a fishing knife that looked weak compared to Marcus’s weapons.
His hands were shaking, but he didn’t give up.
"S-S-Stay back...!" Garrett yelled, his voice breaking.
"I w-won’t let you hurt my wife!"
Rex recognized Garrett as a coward, which led him to believe that taking Mara for himself was the right choice all along.
A woman as beautiful as Mara deserved someone far better than this pathetic man who valued fishing over his wife’s safety.
"Hahahahahaha...!" Marcus laughed, but it was a cold sound that wasn’t funny.
"A fisherman playing the hero, eh?
This will be quick and easy."
He moved forward so quickly that Garrett couldn’t react.
One dagger swept toward the older man’s throat.
Rex’s telekinesis stopped the blade in mid-swing, as if it had hit an invisible wall.
Marcus’s eyes got bigger because he was confused, and then Rex came into view.
"Okay now... that’s far enough," Rex said in a calm voice.
"And it seems like you went overboard with this stupid decision."
Marcus turned to him, and his face lit up with recognition, but then he started to pretend, as he was ordered to by Rex.
"Whoa, hey!
You’re the one who’s been at the hero party!"
"Yeah," Rex said, stepping in front of Marcus and the couple, knowing that Marcus still acted like he didn’t know him from three days ago.
"Garrett, take Mara to the root cellar and lock the door...
Don’t come out until someone from the Starlight family comes to get you."
"But what about you?" Garrett stammered.
"Just get your ass to move now!
I’ll be fine." Rex said while doing stretches.
Mara said.
"Come on, Garrett!
You heard him!"
Mara took her husband’s arm and pulled him to the back of the inn.
They went through a door, and Rex heard a heavy bar slide into place.
Marcus watched them leave, then focused all of his attention on Rex.
It was hard to tell what he was feeling because his face showed both anger and something else.
And it felt like something more personal.
"You know who I am," Rex said, and it wasn’t a question.
"I know you’re in the way," Marcus said, tightening his grip on his daggers.
"Stop with all of this drama now because the boss knew your plan right away by using us all!"
Rex laughed.
"I fucking knew it... and it seems like it was a dumb move to try and stab me in the back anyway.
Rex grinned.
"I think we have more to talk about than you think..."
"Come with me.
I want to show you something."
He turned and walked toward the stairs without looking back to see if Marcus was following.
His foresight told him that curiosity would win out over caution, and sure enough, he heard Marcus’s footsteps behind him.
"What the fuck do you want to show to me...?"
They went up to the second floor, and Rex took him to the room where Lily was.
He knocked once, letting her know that it’s him.
"Come in!" Lily answered right away, and then he opened the door.
Marcus’s body was already in shock hearing those familiar voices coming from the room, and when they enter the room... both of them can see Lily.
Lily was now dressed and sitting on the edge of the bed with her arms around her knees.
When she saw Marcus, her eyes got bigger, and something complicated flashed across her face.
It was recognition, confusion, and a little bit of old pain.
"M-Marcus...?" she said in a quiet voice.
"N-No way..." Marcus stopped in the doorway, and his daggers dropped a little.
"L-Lily?
Is that r-really you..."
"Wait... now I remember... you’re one of them too...
I fucking forgot!" Marcus said while hitting his head softly.
"What are you doing here...?" His eyes moved around the room, taking in the messy bed, Lily’s messy hair, and the close atmosphere.
"W-What the fuck...?"

"Don’t spill that shit on my face...!
You... showing me this, I fucking knew that you are one sly motherfucker!" Marcus said while pointing at him.
Rex shut the door behind them, locking the three of them in the room.
"Well...
Marcus, I didn’t do anything she didn’t want."
Rex glanced at her.
"Isn’t that right, Lily?"
Lily’s face turned red, but she nodded.
"Yes...
I wanted this...
I wanted him."
Marcus looked like he had been hit in the stomach.
"No, you don’t understand this situation at all, Lily...!
You don’t know what you’re saying!"
"He’s controlling you, he’s—"
"I’m sorry, Marcus... but I already fell in love with him," Lily said, her voice getting stronger.
"I love Rex."

chapters.title: Chapter 64. Rejection Hurts, Right?
paragraphs: The words hit Marcus like a punch in the gut. He had to catch himself against the doorframe because his knees buckled a little.
He was about to cry tears of rage, just because of a heartbreak and betrayal.
"Y-You... were supposed to wait for me!" Marcus said with a lot of emotion. "I told you I’d come back for you...!"
"I told you we’d be together one day, and that... was our promise!"
"We were kids back then," Lily said in a soft voice. "That was a long time ago, Marcus..."
"You left me, and now... it seems like you became a bandit." Lily sighed. "Did you really think I’d wait forever for someone who chose that life...?"
Marcus shouted, "I didn’t have any choice to choose that life!"

"My family lost EVERYTHING...! I had to live, I had to—" He stopped, his hands shaking so much that the daggers were rattling. "And you just gave yourself to this... this fucking narcissistic stranger?!"
"A guy you met a few weeks ago?"
"Watch your mouth...! He’s not a random stranger for me," Lily said. "He’s kind and brave, and he really sees me as who I am right now!"
"You really lost it this time, Lily... I didn’t even know you could act like that!" Marcus let all of his anger out on Rex. "YOU...!!!"
"What the FUCK did you do to her!? EXPLAIN TO ME NOW BEFORE I KILL AND TORTURE YOU!!!" Marcus lets out all the voice he has. "WHAT KIND OF SPELL OR CHARM OR—"
Rex said calmly, accompanied by a light laugh, "Such a pointless spell or charm... I don’t need that shit at all."
"There’s nothing like that." Rex raised both his arms while shaking his head. "I just gave her love and attention... things you apparently couldn’t be bothered to give, perhaps."
"YOU FUCKING BASTARD...!!!" Marcus started moving like crazy. "I’LL FUCKING KILL YOU!!!"
Rex’s foresight told him exactly how the attack would happen. Marcus lunged forward, both daggers leading in a complicated double strike that was meant to hit Rex’s heart and throat at the same time.
It was a smart move that came from years of practice and real combat experience.
Additionally, the attack was completely ineffective.

Rex easily avoided the attack because his foresight showed him the exact path of both blades a full second before they got there. His hand shot out and grabbed Marcus’s wrist in the middle of the strike.
He used telekinesis to make his grip stronger until it felt like a steel vise was holding him. "Seems like I hit a nerve, huh?"
"What are you even going to do to me...? Didn’t you remember what happened the three days before?" Rex starts ragebaiting him with a look of someone who has just seen trash.
Marcus tried to break free by slashing at Rex’s face with his other hand, but Rex caught that wrist as well. He maintained an arm’s length distance from Marcus, effortlessly dispelling the threat.
"You’re quick, I’ll give you that, not gonna lie," Rex said. "Well trained too."
"If I’m reading your aura right, you also know earth magic... and you could use it to strengthen your strikes, make platforms to move around on, and maybe even some walls to protect yourself."
Marcus’s eyes got bigger. "How did you—

Rex didn’t say anything. Instead, he used his telekinesis to pull Marcus off balance, pulling him forward and then slamming him into the wall so hard that the plaster cracked. Marcus gasped, the wind knocked out of him, and his daggers fell to the ground.
Lily just watched without intervening, other than being amazed by Rex’s greatness, whereas Marcus felt even more heartbroken when she kept staring at him.
Rex was on him before he could get back up. A telekinetic grip wrapped around Marcus’s throat, lifting him off the ground and holding him against the wall.
Marcus scratched at his own neck, trying to get rid of fingers that weren’t there. "Guuuggghhhh...!!!"
"Let me be very clear this time," Rex said in a low, threatening voice. "Lily is mine..."
"Not because I tricked her or cast a spell, but because I gave her something you never could! I gave her a choice, and she chose me."
"That’s probably enough to solve your heartbreak, right?" Rex laughed.
Marcus wanted to talk, but the pressure on his throat made it impossible. His face was getting red, and the veins in his temples were sticking out.
Rex moved closer and said, "You know what’s funny?"
"You chose the bandit life... and you also chose to attack innocent villages! And now you’re going to pay for those choices."
He let up on the pressure just enough for Marcus to get some air.
"Please," Marcus wheezed. "Let me go...! I’ll leave and never come back."
"Oh, we’re way past that now," Rex said with a smile that didn’t reach his eyes. "And don’t fucking think that I’m stupid enough to let you go."
"I know that you’re trying to snitch." Rex smirks, knowing that his foresight had already told him that Marcus is going to spill the truth that the bandits were because of his plan.
He twisted his hand, and Marcus screamed. His left arm bent back at an odd angle, and the telekinetic force was so strong that it broke his bones and muscles with surgical precision.
In the small room, the sound of breaking bone was loud.
CRACK! CRACK! CRACK!
"AAAAAAGGGGHHHHHHHH!!!"
Lily gasped from the bed and put her hand over her mouth, but she didn’t tell him to stop. She just stood there with her eyes wide open.
Rex turned his attention to Marcus’s other arm and did the same thing again. Another scream, and then a sickening crack.
CRAACCCKKKK!
Marcus’s arms were now uselessly hanging at his sides, broken in several places.
"Magic from the earth, you said?" Rex thought. "Let’s see how well you can concentrate even when it hurts."

Marcus tried hard to bring out his power, and Rex could feel the magical energy building up in his core. But Rex broke his concentration with a sudden spike of pressure against his temples, like invisible hands squeezing his skull from both sides.
Marcus’s scream turned into a howl of pain, and the magic that had been there disappeared without hurting anyone.
"AGGGGGGHHHHHHHH!!!"
"Fucking hell...! Telekinesis is peak," Rex said casually, as if he were talking about the weather instead of hurting someone. "It’s not just about moving things..."
"It’s about putting force on anything, anywhere, like pressure points, organs, or the little bones in your ears that help you keep your balance."
"I fucking knew that this power is underrated and hasn’t been used to its full potential in other fantasy stuff."
He showed by messing with Marcus’s inner ear, and the bandit immediately started to gag, even though he was perfectly still against the wall.
"S-Stop...!" Marcus managed to say between gasps. "Please...! Just end my miserable life... NOW...!!!"
"Nope, I don’t think so," Rex said. "We still have to think about our audience."
Lily moved on the bed at that moment. She was fully awake now because of Marcus’s screams, and she was looking at what was happening in front of her with a mix of horror and something else.
Something that looked a lot like happiness.
"Lily," Marcus said, his eyes finding hers through the pain. "Please...! Tell him to stop...!"
"We used to be childhood friends...! We loved each other!!!"
Lily got up slowly and walked over to where Rex was holding Marcus up. She really looked at her childhood friend, seeing the broken arms, the tears, and the hopelessness.
Then she put her arms around Rex from behind and rested her head on his shoulder.
"I don’t love you at all... Marcus," she said in a low voice. "I don’t think I ever really did..."
"That was just a child’s dream, and now... here I am with someone that I loved the most. Rex is real, and what we have is real."
Marcus’s face fell, and all of his hope left him. Tears ran down his face, mixing with the sweat and blood from where he bit his lip to keep from screaming.
Rex turned his head a little to look at Lily, and the smile he gave her was real. Then he smiled at Marcus again, and this time it turned into something mean and predatory.
"Awww... rejection hurts, right?" Rex laughed.

He snapped his fingers, and the telekinetic force shot out in all directions. Marcus was torn from the wall and hurled across the room, crashing through the door of a small storage closet in the corner.

Rex’s fist was clenched before he could even try to crawl out, and the door slammed shut. The lock clicked, and then Rex used his power to wrap strips of torn fabric around Marcus’s mouth to make sure he couldn’t talk.
The only sounds now were muffled cries and the sound of Marcus kicking the door with his legs, which didn’t work.
"MPPPPHHHHHH!!!"
"That should do it."

chapters.title: Chapter 65. When Your Hired Bandit Becomes a Final Boss
paragraphs: Marcus starts banging on the closet with his legs, but then they get tied as well because of Rex’s telekinesis.
"Shh," Rex told the closet. "You should feel honored to get a chance to live by staying there."
"I’ll take care of you tonight."
He then looked at Lily, who was still holding on to him. "Are you all right, baby?"
She nodded her head against his shoulder. "I should feel bad... and maybe I should feel guilty, but I don’t..."
"Is that bad?"
"Nope," Rex said, running his fingers through her hair. "That’s called moving on."
"You chose yourself over someone who never chose you and doesn’t even recognize who you really are." Rex said while caressing her hair.
She pulled back to look up at him, and her eyes were now fierce. "I love you, Rex... You are the only one who could make me feel special and loved."
"I know," he said, kissing her forehead.
And then...
The sounds of battle were starting to change from the outside. The explosions had stopped, and the screaming was getting more organized.
The fight was almost coming to an end.
"Seems like it’s going to be over soon."
Rex’s Foresight suddenly lit up with a warning, showing him something that made his eyes narrow.
Something was going on in the village square below.
And it’s something risky.
He told Lily. "Stay here, alright? You’re not recovered enough."
"Lock the door. I need to see how your family is doing."
"Be careful," she said.
"I’m always careful," he lied and walked to the window. "Oh... and, Lily."
"Hm?"

"You’re not going to tell your family about what happened today here, right...? And also my real powers... they’re telekinesis." Rex tells her the truth right away. "You know what happens when you snitch on me."
Lily nodded while closing both her eyes and opening them again, where Rex could see heart symbols on both of her eyes. "I won’t tell anyone, Rex..."
"Go save the day, my love." Lily smiled widely while closing both her eyes.
The view from the roof was very different when Rex got there. Less than ten bandits were present now, with the majority injured and fleeing.
It was clear that the Starlight family had won the fight.
But Kruger wasn’t done yet.
The huge bandit leader was surrounded. Elliot stood in front of him, sword raised and breathing hard.
To his left was Evelyn, whose sword was bloody but ready. Diana was on her roof and had an arrow aimed at Kruger’s head.
And Helena was getting ready to cast what looked like a final, overpowered spell. Her hands were crackling with fire and lightning.
Kruger was injured badly. There was an arrow sticking out of his shoulder and one out of his thigh.
There were burns on one side of his face, and a deep sword cut had opened his side so much that Rex could see ribs. The man should have been on the ground, dead.
"That’s enough... you’re better than this." Elliot said, trying to change him. "I know that there’s still some good in you...!"
"My god... this fucking bitch." Rex could see from afar that Elliot was trying to make Kruger change into someone better. "A pussy like this should’ve died sooner with that fucking mindset."

"Fuck all of your words down your throat...! I don’t have anything better inside me other than taking something that I want!"
"You think you’ve won just because of that...!? " Despite his pain, Kruger’s voice remained strong as he shouted. "You think I didn’t plan for any of this!?"
He took a small vial out of his belt. Rex could see liquid sloshing around inside the dark glass.
It was thick and red, almost black, and it looked like it was glowing from the inside.
"What the fuck is that...?"
"No, Kruger! Stop it now!!!" Elliot shouted, knowing it was dangerous even though he didn’t fully understand it. "That thing isn’t worth it!"
"Not worth it? Who are you to talk to me like that, you fucking asshole!" Kruger’s laugh turned insane. "This is...! This is what you called POWEEERRRRR!!!"
Rex’s Foresight was full of warnings, with timeline after timeline showing disaster. Kruger drank the vial in every branch.
And in every branch, what came next was death.
"Ah shit," Rex said, already getting his telekinetic power ready.
Kruger broke the vial against his teeth and drank it.
The effect was immediate and horrifying.
His body shook, and the muscles under his skin bulged and twisted. The wounds that had been bleeding freely suddenly stopped, and the flesh quickly began to knit together.
His eyes rolled back in his head, showing only whites. When they rolled forward again, they were completely black, like pools of oil.
"Everyone back!" Helena screamed. "Get away from him!"
But it was too late. Kruger’s body started to change and mutate.
His skin turned a deep red and felt like cracked stone. His muscles got so big that they ripped through his armor and clothes and became very ugly.
Horns grew out of his head and curled back like a ram’s. His fingers turned into claws, and each one ended in a talon that was as long as a knife blade.
"Holy shit... that looks interesting. " Rex gets more invested just by seeing his transformation from drinking the vial.
Kruger’s teeth had turned into fangs, and the sound that came out of his mouth was not human. It was a deep, loud roar that shook windows and scared crows off of roofs nearby.
"RAAAAAAAGGGGGGHHHHHHHHHHH!!!
It took less than five seconds for the change to happen. Where Kruger had stood, there was now a demon.
It was a creature of pure violence, almost nine feet tall, and its body gave off heat like a forge.
"You’re all fucked now...!!!" Kruger said with a big terrifying smile.
Elliot tried to charge it anyway. "For the people and justice...!"

His Heroic Strike went off, and his sword glowed with golden light as he swung it at the demon’s body. The sword hit with a sound, like metal hitting metal, and the impact sent shockwaves through the square.
The demon didn’t even move.
It hit Elliot in the back of the head and sent him flying. He crashed through the wall of a nearby store and vanished in a cloud of dust and debris.
"Elliot!" Evelyn screamed and moved to fight.
She was very fast, faster than any human could ever be, thanks to her speed. She blurred as she circled the demon, making cuts at every exposed point she could find.
Her sword drew blood, dark ichor that hissed when it hit the ground, but the wounds healed almost as quickly as she made them.
The demon’s hand moved faster than it should have been able to, and it grabbed Evelyn by the leg. It picked her up off the ground and slammed her down hard enough to break the cobblestones.
"GAGGHH...!!!" She gasped, the wind leaving her lungs, and the demon raised its clawed hand to kill her.
But then... she was saved because Diana’s arrow hit it in the eye.

The demon screamed in pain and rage, dropping Evelyn and scratching its face. The arrow had gone deep, but Rex could see it being pushed back out by tissue that was growing back as he watched through his Foresight.
Helena cast the spell she had been working on. "Flame Lightning Storm!"
The attack from both sides was devastating. Lightning bolts fell from the sky, each one leaving a trail of fire as they hit the demon in a storm of elemental rage.
The demon was swallowed up, and its screams of pain were drowned out by the loud explosions.
The demon was still standing when the spell was over. Its skin was burned and smoking, and one arm was hanging at a strange angle, but it was getting better.
The burned skin was already peeling off, showing new skin underneath.
It grinned at Helena with too many teeth and black eyes. "You fucking bitch...!"
Then it ran at her.
Rex watched from the roof, his mind racing. The Starlight family was outmatched.
The demon was getting stronger faster than they could hurt it, and it was too strong for them to handle. He could see timelines in his Foresight where Helena died, Diana died, and everyone else died.
He should step in so that he could change things like he always does to gain their trust. His telekinesis could hold the demon back long enough for the others to regroup and maybe find a weak spot.
But if he did that, people would ask questions about how powerful he really was. His carefully crafted image would start to fall apart.
"Alright... seems like it gets difficult here because of that vial. I didn’t expect that at all."

Rex was about to make that choice. He observed the demon drawing nearer to Helena, observed her preparing for a final attempt to save herself, and observed the branching timelines approaching the brink of catastrophe.
And he grinned.
"Alright, fuck it!" He said to himself, "This will be interesting."
The demon’s clawed hand came down toward Helena’s head.

chapters.title: Chapter 66. I’m Sorry I’m Late, I Was Protecting Lily (Lie)
paragraphs: The demon’s clawed hand was already moving, cutting through the air so quickly that there was no room for error. Helena had her arms up, and a barrier spell was forming around her hands.
But Rex could see through his foresight that the barrier wouldn’t hold. Not against something that had just ruined Helena’s Flame Lightning Storm without a second thought.
Rex did what he had to do right away.
"Fuck it... here goes nothing!"

He used his telekinesis to grab the demon’s arm in the middle of a swing from the roof, putting as much force into the hold as he could, and the effect was instant. Kruger’s arm came to a halt, seemingly trapped in a vise, and he ceased his forward movement less than a foot away from Helena’s face.
The demon growled and looked up with its black eyes, looking for the person who had stopped it.
Helena stumbled back, gasping, and her barrier spell broke when she realized she didn’t need it. She saw Rex on the roof, and her face showed a mix of relief and confusion.
"R-Rex...?" Helena didn’t ask any questions inside her head, but she was relieved that someone had helped.
Rex didn’t give the demon time to get its bearings. He looked around the ruined square and began to make a list of everything he could see.

There were pieces of broken stone from walls that had fallen down, uprooted fence posts, a piece of wood from a cart that had been destroyed, and the thick trunk of a decorative oak tree that had been half-knocked over by the explosions that happened earlier.
Everything turned into bullets.
He pulled with both hands, so to speak, using the full range of his telekinetic powers. The piece of wood rose first and spun once before Rex drove it into the demon’s back like a battering ram.
The sound of the impact was like a tree falling in a forest, and it sent Kruger stumbling forward three full steps.
"This seems fun enough to play with that." Rex smirks.
Before the demon could get up, Rex threw three broken stone slabs from the square’s rubble. The first hit Kruger in the shoulder and turned him to the side.

The second hit him in the ribs, and the sound of breaking bones could be heard even from the roof. The third hit him right in the head, and the force was so strong that a normal person would have broken their neck.
Kruger fell down. He didn’t fall, but he did stagger, and his regeneration was clearly working harder than before to keep up with the damage that was happening.
Rex pushed harder. He grabbed the half-fallen oak tree and pulled it completely out of the ground, roots and all, sending a cloud of dirt into the air.
The tree was by far the heaviest thing he had tried to lift since he unlocked telekinesis. He could feel the strain of it pulling at the edges of his focus, but it held.
The tree swung in a wide arc and hit Kruger in the side like a huge club, knocking him completely off his feet.
Kruger was on the ground for a short time.
"Grrggghhhhh...!!! BASTARDSSSS...!!!" Kruger knew what was attacking him, but he still couldn’t prove it.
Diana took that chance without being told. Three arrows flew in quick succession, each one hitting the demon’s exposed throat, where the skin was a little thinner than the rest.
They drew the dark ichor that served as blood, and Kruger roared as he tried to claw them out.
By that time, Helena had gotten her balance back. While the demon was still clawing at his throat, she shot a bunch of Ice Shards at him.
The frozen projectiles hit his arms and chest, slowing down his regeneration just enough to make a difference.
But just barely enough...
Kruger put one huge hand on the cobblestones and pushed himself up. The arrows had already come out of his healing throat.
He shook himself like a wet dog, sending things flying all over the place. The wounds from the stone slabs were healing.
The bruises from the wood were already going away. It sounded like the tree had broken three of his ribs, but they were slowly coming back together with loud pops.
"EVERYTHING YOU DID TO ME...!!! IT’S ALL...!!! USELESSSSS!!!" Kruger screamed.

Rex watched the regeneration with squinted eyes. He had hoped that hitting the demon with a lot of damage in a short amount of time would stop its healing ability, giving the others enough time to find a real weak point.
It looked like Kruger’s body was getting better faster the more damage it took.
He realized that he needed to approach things differently this time.
"Hey, system, is that what my infinite regeneration would be if I get one?" Rex asked the system first.
[YES! OP!]
"That makes me motivated to raise their desire in this situation then." Rex cracked both his fists. "Alright, let’s just do it!"

Rex jumped off the roof and used his telekinesis to soften his landing in the middle of the square. When he stood up straight, dust flew up around his feet, and the sound of his arrival made everyone turn to look at him.
Elliot looked like he had seen a ghost. "Rex?! What are you doing here?! I thought you were—"
"Protecting Lily," Rex said, cutting him off before the question could get out of hand. "She’s safe... for now."
"She’s locked in her room..." He looked around at the state of the group and made an appropriate apologetic face. "I’m sorry that I’m late."
"I heard that she was attacked by a bandit, and I had to make sure no one got to her first."
Helena smiled in relief. "Thank you, Rex... I appreciate that a lot of you protect Lily."
"It’s okay." Rex nodded.
It was a completely reasonable reason for his absence, and it connected his late arrival to something that would resonate with everyone in the Starlight family.
Lily was one of them. He would always put her safety first.
Elliot began to say something else, but when he tried to move forward, his leg gave out. He caught himself on a broken wall and was breathing through his teeth.
Rex could see the blood soaking through his shirt from where he had crashed through the shop wall. Kruger’s backhand had hurt a lot.
The impact left Kruger with a few broken ribs, possibly a dislocated shoulder, and a full-body ache that lasted for days.
Kruger laughed in a low, wet voice from thirty meters away. His black eyes were fixed on Rex with a new kind of interest.
"Would you look at that!? Another shit comes out of hiding!
Rex didn’t pay attention to him and went back to the group. Helena was standing, but she looked pale.
It was clear that her magical reserves were low from all the casting. Diana had come down from the roof and was standing close to Evelyn.
Evelyn appeared to be the most intact of the four, but she continued to roll her shoulder, suggesting that Kruger’s ground slam had caused more damage than she was admitting.
Rex looked straight at Evelyn. "Are you feeling alright...? Can you still keep going?"
"I’m fine."
"I need your help then."
She looked him in the eye, and he could tell she was thinking. "Do you have a plan?"
"It’s quite simple, actually. You and I fight Kruger head-on while Helena and Diana hit him from a distance with everything they have."
"We keep him moving and off balance so his regeneration doesn’t have a chance to catch up."
"And what if that doesn’t work?" Evelyn asked.
"We think of something else." Rex replied, "But I would prefer to attempt the simple method first rather than die trying."
Evelyn nodded slowly. She was already getting into a better position, reading the battlefield like a reincarnator with combat experience would.
Rex put it away after noting how well it worked. "Alright, let’s also look out for each other."
Rex looked at Diana and Helena. "I need both of you two to support us with every range attack that you two have to slow his regeneration or maybe... cancel out his attacks."
Elliot, as expected, tried to stand up straighter. "I’m fighting too."
"No," Rex said, and he said it in a way that made it clear he didn’t want to hear any more. "You’re injured, Elliot."
"If you go back in there, you’ll die, and that won’t help anyone." Rex tried so hard not to roast him after every word he spoke.
Elliot’s pride and common sense were clearly at odds with each other, and it was a closer fight than Rex would have liked. Evelyn then put her hand on Elliot’s arm for a moment, and his face changed.
"He’s right," she said softly.
Elliot blew out through his nose and then looked at Rex with a look that was almost respectful. "Okay... but I’m not going to sit here and do nothing."
Rex said, "Then give me your sword."
He was surprised by that.
Elliot blinked. "My sword?"
Rex said, "Mine’s upstairs," which was a lie, but it made sense because he hadn’t been carrying one when he came down from the roof.
"I can’t fight that thing with my bare hands."
