"I’m telling you that what you did to Marcus was child’s play compared to what you’ll be capable of once you fully understand your new abilities." Lustia stood again, and this time when she approached him, it was with purpose.
"But we don’t have much time left."
"Your body is waking up in the real world, and if your soul isn’t back by then, things will get complicated."
She reached up and held his face in her hands.
Her touch was warm and surprisingly soft.
"Go back, Rex Rexilion..."

"Go back to the world and show them what an Apostle of Lust can do, and also... take what you want, break what stands in your way, and make me proud until you can come back here again so I can give you more gifts that are worthy of your achievement."
"My system will keep you in check as always, so..."
Then she kissed him, but it wasn’t the hot passion of the ritual; it was something else.
A seal, a contract, a promise made real.
When she pulled back, her smile was soft, but her eyes were raged.
"Do a good job hunting, my dear Apostle."
And then the world around him fell apart.

chapters.title: Chapter 87. New Day, New Power-Up, New Problem Named Theo
paragraphs: Rex’s eyes snapped open to chaos.

Sunlight was streaming through the carriage windows, far too bright for the pre-dawn hour when he’d fallen asleep. His body felt different, charged with energy that hadn’t been there before, and the mark on his right hand pulsed once before settling into dormancy.
Outside the carriage, he can hear someone screaming.
Rex sat up quickly and automatically took stock of his surroundings. Lily was pressed against the back wall of the carriage, and her face was pale.
Helena held her hands up, and magic crackled between them. Diana was looking for a weapon that wasn’t there because everything was packed tightly for the trip.
Evelyn was right behind Elliot, and he was already trying to push open the carriage door. She looked like she was ready to fight.
"What’s going on...?" Rex asked, his voice cutting through the fear.
"Demons," Helena said in a short way. "Flying demons."
"They suddenly appeared five minutes ago."
Rex went to the window and looked out.

The carriage convoy had stopped in what looked like a cleared area next to the road, most likely for a planned break. The soldiers made a loose circle around the four carriages, which were in a loose circle.
Above them, there were at least a dozen clearly demon-like flying creatures, circling like raptors.

These demons were not the little imps that Rex had read about in fantasy books. These were real war beasts, each the size of a horse, with leathery wings, sharp teeth, and riders who looked like they had just come out of a nightmare.

The demons had a reptilian appearance, resembling a hybrid of dragons and wyverns. Their riders wore dark armor covered in symbols that Rex’s new and improved vision quickly recognized as demonic script.
One of the demons turned sharply and dove toward the carriage convoy. Its rider raised a spear that glowed with sickly green energy.
Rex’s Foresight kicked in on its own and showed him the path. The spear was going to hit the wagon.
The carriage they rode in. In about three seconds.
He didn’t think, but he just acted right away.

His telekinesis reached out, unseen and exact, and caught the spear in midair. The weapon halted as if it had collided with a wall, hovering in midair for a brief moment before Rex altered its trajectory.
It then spun off into the woods, where it hit a tree trunk with a blast of corrupted magic.
The demon rider pulled up quickly, and its ugly face showed that it was confused.
"Everyone out," Rex said. "We’re more vulnerable when we’re stuck in here looking all confused. (like a fucking wimp)"
They got out of the carriage and into a mess of organized chaos. Theo was already fighting one of the flying demons.

His huge shield blocked dark magic blasts while he directed the soldiers’ defensive formation. Iris was on top of one of the carriages, bow in hand, shooting arrows at any demon that flew too low with perfect accuracy.

The Starlight family automatically fell into formation, years of fighting experience winning over fear. Helena started casting, and her magic made a protective dome over the people who were huddled near the center carriage.
Diana got her bow and quiver from the supply cart and went up to Iris right away. Elliot took out his sword and went to help Theo.
Evelyn’s supernatural speed propelled her into the fight, enabling her to strike demons as they fell.

Rex stood in the middle of it all, his Foresight showing him every attack before it happened. His telekinesis worked hard to deflect, redirect, and sometimes even crush threats that were coming his way.
While he was tracking six different paths at once, his system woke up with notifications he’d never seen before.
[WELCOME, APOSTLE OF LUST]
[MARK OF LUST AUTHORITY: ACTIVE]
[SYSTEM UPGRADE COMPLETE]
[NEW FEATURES UNLOCKED]
[DETECTION PROTOCOL ACTIVE]
[SCANNING AREA FOR COMPATIBLE TARGETS AND POTENTIAL THREATS]
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: THEO MORR NIGHTWING]
[CLASSIFICATION: APOSTLE OF LIFE - RANK: SQUIRE]
[THREAT LEVEL: MODERATE]
[SYSTEM BLESSING: SHIELD OF VALOR (DEFENSIVE ENHANCEMENT SYSTEM)]
[RECOMMENDATION: MONITOR. DO NOT ENGAGE WHILE MARKED IDENTITY IS ACTIVE.]
Rex’s eyes found Theo across the battlefield, and he could see him more clearly than ever. So Diana’s crush was one of the Goddess of Life’s favorites—what a plot twist already for him.
And that was both useful information and a problem that he would have to deal with carefully.
But then, the system wasn’t finished.
[CONGRATULATIONS ON YOUR ASCENSION]
[YOU ARE NOW RECOGNIZED AS APOSTLE OF LUST]
[NEW ABILITIES AVAILABLE]
[THE LUSTFUL VILLAIN FORM: ACCESSIBLE]
[ENHANCED DESIRE MANIPULATION: ACTIVE]
[PSYCHOLOGICAL DOMINANCE PROTOCOLS: UPGRADED]
[LUST AUTHORITY MARK: OPERATIONAL]
Rex felt a dark sense of satisfaction wash over him. Everything Lustia said would happen did happen and worked.
He could feel the new skills humming just below the surface of his mind, waiting to be used.
But now was not the time to try new things. It was time to end this fight and keep his cover, as he usually does.

He used his telekinesis to grab one of the diving demons by the wings and slam it into the ground so hard that it made a crater. The rider was thrown clear, and soldiers quickly surrounded him and killed him.

The fight went on for a few more minutes, but the outcome was never in doubt. The demons were killed one by one thanks to Theo’s defensive coordination, Iris and Diana’s precise archery, Evelyn’s speed, Helena’s magic, and Rex’s help that was hidden.
When the last one fell, three of Diana’s arrows hit it at once, and the clearing became eerily quiet.
Theo quickly went to the few demons that had lived through their crashes, sword in hand and a hard look on his face. Rex got closer because he was interested in what would happen next.
"That’s enough, you lowly demons! Tell us who sent you here!" Theo shouted, putting his sword to the throat of the demon rider who was still alive.
The creature made a wet, rough laugh. "The Lord Mordecai sends his greetings, Shield Bearer."
"He knows the capital is strengthening its defenses, the Apostles are gathering, and your goddess is getting more and more desperate."
"Mordecai," Theo said again, his voice cold. "You’ll tell me everything about his plans, operations, and locations.
"Like hell I would! I’ll tell you nothing, holy fool." The demon spit black blood at Theo’s feet. "We’re already dead, and you haven’t won anything."
Theo’s face stayed the same. "Then you’ve lived longer than you should have."
The sword moved with deadly precision, and the demon’s head came off before it could do anything. Theo moved on to the next living demon and did the same thing, slowly and without mercy.
All of the demon prisoners were dead within two minutes.
Rex was interested in this show of practical violence. So the brave Apostle of Life wasn’t against killing enemies who had already lost.
That was helpful to know how far his morals really went.
"Rex!"
He turned to see Lily running toward him with a look of relief on her face. Without thinking, she threw her arms around him, and he automatically caught her, putting his hands on her waist.
He smiled a little and said, "Good morning to you too."
"I was so worried! You were still sleeping when it started, and I thought you might be hurt because of the sudden attack..."
"Then the spear almost hit us, and I..." She pulled back just enough to look at him. "Are you all right?"
"I’m fine." Rex told her, "Apparently, I just woke up at the wrong time."
Helena came closer, and her face showed how difficult it had been to keep that protective dome up for so long. "Sorry for waking you up so suddenly."
"Without any warning or scouts, the demons suddenly appeared. It was a planned attack."
Theo joined them and said, "It was supposed to be a probing attack."
He had blood on his armor, but other than that, he looked fine. "They wanted to see how well we could defend ourselves and maybe kill some of us to lower our spirits before we got to the capital."
"They mentioned Mordecai," Rex said. "Is that the demon lord Iris told us about?"
"Yeah, the same." Theo looked very serious. "This confirms what we know."
"He’s actively trying to stop the Apostle gathering that Lady Valentina has called for by moving people to Aethelgard."
Evelyn appeared beside Elliot, breathing only slightly harder than normal despite having just fought a small war. "Are the civilians alright?"
"They’re shaken but unharmed," Helena said.
Evelyn smiled. "As always... your barrier held up perfectly, Mother."
Rex thought it was interesting that she used "Mother" instead of Helena’s name and put it away. The family situation was more complicated than he had thought at first.
"We should keep going," Iris said from her place on top of the carriage. "These were scouts."
"There could be more coming, and I’d rather be inside the walls of the capital when that happens."
Theo nodded. "Agreed."
"Everyone back to the carriages. If we hurry, we’ll be in Aethelgard in two hours."
"I want to get there as quickly as possible."

As they start to walk back to the carriage, Rex starts to have some negative thoughts about what Theo and the demon just said about ’Apostle gathering.’ It made him think that the apostle thing was a common thing that he wanted to ask later to one of them.
For now, he just needs to keep as low a profile as possible and use the Lustful Villain form soon when the right time has come.

chapters.title: Chapter 88. Nine Devoted Women and a Pretty Face. (My To-Do List Just Got Longer.)
paragraphs: The group started to get back together. Soldiers cleared demon bodies from the road, and civilians got back into the carriages.
Rex was back in the same carriage as before, but this time the mood was much more tense.
Rex sat quietly and let his mind work through everything that had happened while they continued their journey. He had gotten godlike powers from a real goddess when he woke up.
He had lived through an attack by a demon. He had found one of the Goddess of Life’s Apostles among the people he was traveling with.
And he was about to go into a big city that, if Lustia’s warnings were true, would be full of both chances and dangers.
Lily was pressed against his side again. Her fear had changed into a need for physical comfort.
He let her stay there with one arm around her shoulders while he thought about what to do next. The mark on his hand pulsed once, so faint that only he could feel it, and he smiled.
The landscape changed as they traveled, becoming more cultivated and less wild. Farmland appeared, worked by people who stopped their labor to watch the carriage convoy pass.
Small villages dotted the roadside, each one looking prosperous and well-maintained in a way that spoke to effective governance and security.
Then, as they reached the top of a final hill, they finally saw Aethelgard.
Rex had seen large cities before, both in his previous life and in the brief time he’d spent in this world. However, Aethelgard was a completely different experience.
The outer ring was made up of what looked like permanent settlements, with dozens of villages that had grown together to make a huge suburban network. These weren’t slums or shacks.
There were real communities with real roads, stone buildings, and what looked like organized infrastructure.
And the wall rose up behind them, like a monument to civilization itself. It was at least a hundred feet tall and made of white stone that glowed softly in the afternoon sun.
At regular intervals along its length, guard towers stood out, each one manned by soldiers whose armor caught the light. The main gate was huge; it could fit three carriages side by side.
On either side of it were statues of what Rex thought were historical figures or maybe gods.
As their convoy approached, the gates began to open, massive mechanisms moving with smooth precision that suggested both magic and engineering working in harmony.
The guards knew Theo right away and waved him through without doing the usual security checks. The convoy drove through the gate and into the real capital.
The interior was just as impressive as the exterior promised it would be. Big streets paved with something that looked like marble but was probably stronger.

The city was filled with a mix of practical buildings, such as stores and homes, alongside impressive architectural wonders that reached six or seven stories high. People bustled about with determination, dressed in various attire that ranged from simple work garments to elaborate outfits befitting nobility.
And there was a building that stood out from the rest of the skyline and made everything else look small.

The building combined elements of a castle, a cathedral, and a wizard’s tower, making it difficult to categorize. It was huge, at least fifteen stories high, and had many wings and towers that branched off from a central structure.
The architecture was both beautiful and intimidating, and every surface seemed to have decorative elements that served both aesthetic and probably magical purposes.
"That’s the Academy," Helena said, seeing where Rex was looking. "The Grand Academy of Magical Arts and Combat.
"It’s the best academy of its kind in the whole world."
Rex said, "That’s actually kind of impressive," and he meant it.
"It’s where I learned everything about magic that the road couldn’t teach me," Helena said. "It’s where Diana honed her archery skills with masters who had been doing it for fifty years."
"And it’s also where Elliot learned how to use a sword from real-life legendary heroes." She stopped. "That’s also where you’ll probably end up if you stay in Aethelgard for a while."
"They have programs just for reincarnators to help you get better at what you do." She said that while whispering at him.
Rex put that information away because it was crucial. The academy was teeming with talented individuals, many likely reincarnators with unique systems and advantages, all gathered in one location.
It could have been a target-rich environment or a minefield, depending on how he played it.

The convoy moved through the city streets, taking a route that seemed to avoid the busiest areas. They strolled by bustling marketplaces, neighborhoods with children playing in courtyards, and government buildings inhabited by individuals who appeared to be employees.
Finally, they reached a big plaza in front of the academy.
The carriages came to a stop, and people began disembarking.
Theo quickly began working with other soldiers who had come to meet them. He ensured the correct distribution of supplies and relocated the civilian refugees to temporary housing.
Iris stepped in to help, and her natural efficiency made her a valuable part of the organized chaos.
Rex got out of the carriage and stood still for a moment, taking in his surroundings and letting his enhanced senses stretch out.
That’s when his body went completely crazy.
[DETECTION PROTOCOL: MULTIPLE REINCARNATORS IN RANGE]
[PROCESSING]
[PROCESSING]
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: ACADEMY STUDENT, CLASSIFICATION: UNKNOWN]
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: ADVENTURER, CLASSIFICATION: UNKNOWN]
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: MERCHANT, CLASSIFICATION: UNKNOWN]
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: ACADEMY STUDENT, CLASSIFICATION: UNKNOWN]
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: ACADEMY STUDENT, CLASSIFICATION: UNKNOWN]
The alerts kept coming, a steady stream of detections that showed just how full Aethelgard was of souls that had come back to life, and there were a lot of them.
They’re walking around, going to study and learn at the academy, running businesses, and being guards. There are dozens, maybe hundreds, of them in the area.
"Holy fucking hell... there are many shitholes everywhere, and it seems like this place really does need some genocide." Rex thought to himself.
Most of them were basic reincarnators, people who had been given a second chance but didn’t have anything special to offer other than what they learned in their past lives.
Some showed signs of small system blessings, which are small advantages that would help but not make them powerful.
And then, cutting through all the noise in the background, one detection brought Rex’s full attention to the task at hand.
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: APOLLO BRIGHTSOUL]
[CLASSIFICATION: APOSTLE OF LIFE - RANK: PALADIN]
[THREAT LEVEL: EXTREME]
[SYSTEM BLESSING: HAREM KING PROTOCOL + DIVINE FAVOR (GODDESS OF LIFE)]
[CURRENT HAREM COUNT: 9 BONDED]
[OBSERVATION: TARGET IS SURROUNDED BY DEVOTED FOLLOWERS, RECEIVES POWER BOOST FROM THEIR FAITH AND LOVE]
[RECOMMENDATION: PRIORITY ELIMINATION TARGET - EXTREME CAUTION ADVISED]
Rex’s eyes automatically found the target after following the system’s directional ping.

There was a young man standing in the plaza near the main entrance to the academy. His appearance suggested that someone had crafted him based on a list of qualities essential for a compelling protagonist.
He was tall but not scary, and he had golden blonde hair and blue eyes that sparkled in the sun. He was good-looking in a way that was almost generic.
His armor was both useful and attractive. It was white and gold with symbols that Rex recognized as belonging to the Goddess of Life.
Nine women, including a young woman and an older woman, were arranged in a loose semicircle around him. They looked both protective and loving at the same time.
Each one was beautiful in her own special way. One of them was a warrior woman, characterized by her red hair and fierce eyes. A mage donned elaborate robes adorned with mysterious symbols.
There was also a healer, dressed in white and silver, who seemed to have the power to heal people simply by smiling. An archer with elvish looks and grace that can’t be explained.
And five more, each one clearly devoted to the golden-haired main character in the middle.
Rex saw Apollo Brightsoul laugh at something one of the women said. His face was open and warm, and there was no sign of darkness or doubt.
The women laughed back, and their faces lit up with real happiness, like flowers turning toward the sun.
This sight was disgusting to him, yet it was precisely what Rex had been seeking.
An apostle of life, blessed by the goddess who had tried to punish Rex for his sins. He was a harem protagonist who grew stronger through love and devotion, rather than through desire or obsession.
This rival personified everything that Rex detested about the pure, ethically sound form of power that the Goddess of Life favored.
And the best part was that Lustia had told him to kill this person.
Rex’s smile was predatory, not warm.
He had found his main goal in Aethelgard. And he was already excited to see Apollo Brightsoul’s perfect little world go up in flames.

Big streets paved with something that looked like marble but was probably stronger.
The city was filled with a mix of practical buildings, such as stores and homes, alongside impressive architectural wonders that reached six or seven stories high.
People bustled about with determination, dressed in various attire that ranged from simple work garments to elaborate outfits befitting nobility.
And there was a building that stood out from the rest of the skyline and made everything else look small.
The building combined elements of a castle, a cathedral, and a wizard’s tower, making it difficult to categorize.
It was huge, at least fifteen stories high, and had many wings and towers that branched off from a central structure.
The architecture was both beautiful and intimidating, and every surface seemed to have decorative elements that served both aesthetic and probably magical purposes.
"That’s the Academy," Helena said, seeing where Rex was looking.
"The Grand Academy of Magical Arts and Combat.
"It’s the best academy of its kind in the whole world."
Rex said, "That’s actually kind of impressive," and he meant it.
"It’s where I learned everything about magic that the road couldn’t teach me," Helena said.
"It’s where Diana honed her archery skills with masters who had been doing it for fifty years."
"And it’s also where Elliot learned how to use a sword from real-life legendary heroes." She stopped.
"That’s also where you’ll probably end up if you stay in Aethelgard for a while."
"They have programs just for reincarnators to help you get better at what you do." She said that while whispering at him.
Rex put that information away because it was crucial.
The academy was teeming with talented individuals, many likely reincarnators with unique systems and advantages, all gathered in one location.
It could have been a target-rich environment or a minefield, depending on how he played it.
The convoy moved through the city streets, taking a route that seemed to avoid the busiest areas.
They strolled by bustling marketplaces, neighborhoods with children playing in courtyards, and government buildings inhabited by individuals who appeared to be employees.
Finally, they reached a big plaza in front of the academy.
The carriages came to a stop, and people began disembarking.
Theo quickly began working with other soldiers who had come to meet them.
He ensured the correct distribution of supplies and relocated the civilian refugees to temporary housing.
Iris stepped in to help, and her natural efficiency made her a valuable part of the organized chaos.
Rex got out of the carriage and stood still for a moment, taking in his surroundings and letting his enhanced senses stretch out.
That’s when his body went completely crazy.
[DETECTION PROTOCOL: MULTIPLE REINCARNATORS IN RANGE]
[PROCESSING]
[PROCESSING]
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: ACADEMY STUDENT, CLASSIFICATION: UNKNOWN]
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: ADVENTURER, CLASSIFICATION: UNKNOWN]
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: MERCHANT, CLASSIFICATION: UNKNOWN]
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: ACADEMY STUDENT, CLASSIFICATION: UNKNOWN]
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: ACADEMY STUDENT, CLASSIFICATION: UNKNOWN]
The alerts kept coming, a steady stream of detections that showed just how full Aethelgard was of souls that had come back to life, and there were a lot of them.
They’re walking around, going to study and learn at the academy, running businesses, and being guards.
There are dozens, maybe hundreds, of them in the area.
"Holy fucking hell... there are many shitholes everywhere, and it seems like this place really does need some genocide." Rex thought to himself.
Most of them were basic reincarnators, people who had been given a second chance but didn’t have anything special to offer other than what they learned in their past lives.
Some showed signs of small system blessings, which are small advantages that would help but not make them powerful.
And then, cutting through all the noise in the background, one detection brought Rex’s full attention to the task at hand.
[REINCARNATOR DETECTED: APOLLO BRIGHTSOUL]
[CLASSIFICATION: APOSTLE OF LIFE - RANK: PALADIN]
[THREAT LEVEL: EXTREME]
[SYSTEM BLESSING: HAREM KING PROTOCOL + DIVINE FAVOR (GODDESS OF LIFE)]
[CURRENT HAREM COUNT: 9 BONDED]
[OBSERVATION: TARGET IS SURROUNDED BY DEVOTED FOLLOWERS, RECEIVES POWER BOOST FROM THEIR FAITH AND LOVE]
[RECOMMENDATION: PRIORITY ELIMINATION TARGET - EXTREME CAUTION ADVISED]
Rex’s eyes automatically found the target after following the system’s directional ping.
There was a young man standing in the plaza near the main entrance to the academy.
His appearance suggested that someone had crafted him based on a list of qualities essential for a compelling protagonist.
He was tall but not scary, and he had golden blonde hair and blue eyes that sparkled in the sun.
He was good-looking in a way that was almost generic.
His armor was both useful and attractive.
It was white and gold with symbols that Rex recognized as belonging to the Goddess of Life.
Nine women, including a young woman and an older woman, were arranged in a loose semicircle around him.
They looked both protective and loving at the same time.
Each one was beautiful in her own special way.
One of them was a warrior woman, characterized by her red hair and fierce eyes.
A mage donned elaborate robes adorned with mysterious symbols.
There was also a healer, dressed in white and silver, who seemed to have the power to heal people simply by smiling.
An archer with elvish looks and grace that can’t be explained.
And five more, each one clearly devoted to the golden-haired main character in the middle.
Rex saw Apollo Brightsoul laugh at something one of the women said.
His face was open and warm, and there was no sign of darkness or doubt.
The women laughed back, and their faces lit up with real happiness, like flowers turning toward the sun.
This sight was disgusting to him, yet it was precisely what Rex had been seeking.
An apostle of life, blessed by the goddess who had tried to punish Rex for his sins.
He was a harem protagonist who grew stronger through love and devotion, rather than through desire or obsession.
This rival personified everything that Rex detested about the pure, ethically sound form of power that the Goddess of Life favored.
And the best part was that Lustia had told him to kill this person.
Rex’s smile was predatory, not warm.
He had found his main goal in Aethelgard.
And he was already excited to see Apollo Brightsoul’s perfect little world go up in flames.

paragraphs: When Theo stepped forward and spoke to the group, the plaza in front of the Grand Academy was still full of organized chaos. His voice had the kind of authority that comes from years of training as a leader.
His voice effortlessly penetrated the surrounding noise.
"Okay, everyone, listen up," he said, and right away the conversations that were going on stopped.
"Iris and I need to work with the city guard, file reports on the demon attack, and make sure that all the civilian refugees are properly registered and housed before anyone can really settle in."

Iris nodded next to him, already looking around the area like a professional who was mentally making a list of things to do. "Sorting through everything will probably take us most of the afternoon, if not... longer than usual, considering how many civilians there are."

Helena stepped forward, and her body language changed to show that she was taking on a new role, one that was more formal than the traveling mage she had been for the past few days. "I’ll take Elliot, Diana, Lily, Evelyn, and Rex to the Academy..."
"My mother will be waiting for us, and there are things that can’t wait."

When she said "Mother," Rex noticed a small change in her tone that showed respect and something else that he couldn’t quite put his finger on yet. It’s maybe duty, perhaps. Or it might be the pressure that came with being the daughter of someone important for the whole capital.
"Alright, perfect," Theo said. "We’ll meet up again tonight at the Nightwing estate."

"My mother will want to see everyone, and I know Grandmother and Great Grandmother will be impossible to deal with if they don’t get their reunion." He said the last part with a mix of love and annoyance that made it clear this was a common situation.

Rex’s attention was then fully focused when Theo mentioned "mother," "grandmother," and "great-grandmother." So Rex could see and take his family’s many baddies to increase his desire energy even more.
Rex thought to himself. "I fucking knew it... this capital is going to be the best unlimited source of desire energy regeneration. Knowing there are two families, that’s probably important..."
"The Starlights and the Nightwings..."
"Oh, shit! I forgot!" Iris laughed.
"What?" Theo looked at her.
"I’ve been ignoring Aurelia’s three crystal communication messages asking when we’d get there."
"Oh my god... you’re a coward as always facing her, huh," Theo said calmly.
"She always asks for some sparring! You do know that I can win against pure brute force for a fighter knight like her!"
"Yeah, yeah, yeah."

After that, Theo and Iris left with a group of soldiers, and Helena told her group to follow. Rex walked up next to Lily, who was looking around with wide eyes that made it look like she hadn’t been to the capital in a long time, if ever.
"Are you excited?" Rex asked softly.
"Not quite; it’s more that I’m nervous about seeing my grandmother after a very long time." Lily said, "Grandmother Valentina is great, but she can also be scary when she wants to be."
Rex put that information away for later use and followed Helena to the academy’s main entrance.

When they arrived at the academy’s main entrance, Rex knew that it was even more impressive up close. The doors were at least twenty feet tall and made of dark wood that had been polished until it shone.

They were covered in complicated designs that Rex’s enhanced perception recognized as functional enchantments layered over decorative art. The intricate designs included protection wards, detection spells, and what appeared to be a significant amount of magic to regulate entry.
Without thinking, Helena walked up and put her hand on a certain spot on the door. Magic flared up for a moment, a soft golden light that followed the lines of her palm.
Then the doors opened on their own.
Rick muttered. ’It has some kind of scanner magic, huh? Interesting.’
The entrance hall beyond was huge and beautiful. Columns of white marble with gold veins held up the ceiling, which was at least four stories high.

Big windows let in natural light that somehow made it brighter and softer at the same time, making the room feel bright without being too bright. Students moved around in small groups, and their conversations were a low hum of academic talk and casual talk.

Rex’s system started keeping track of reincarnators right away, but he turned off the notifications because he didn’t want to be distracted by how many there were. He would have time later to figure out who was worth his time.
"This way," Helena said, pointing them to a big staircase that curved up the wall. "Mother’s office is on the top floor because she likes to see everything when she’s done with her work."
They climbed in silence, passing floors that branched off into hallways with doors that probably led to classrooms, labs, and places to live.
Everyone they passed, both students and teachers, seemed to know Helena. They bowed or greeted her in a respectful way, and she did the same in a professional way.
Rex had counted fifteen stories by the time they got to the top floor. He was really impressed with how big the building was and how easily he climbed it without getting out of breath.
His stronger body made what should have been arduous work seem effortless.
The top floor was not like the others. The lower levels had felt busy and academic, but this area was quiet and meant to be intimidating.

A long hallway stretched out in front of them, with portraits on the walls that Rex thought were of past Academy heads or important historical figures. The smaller double doors at the other end were made of the same dark wood as the entrance.
Helena stopped in front of them, took a breath that made it seem like she was getting her thoughts together, and then knocked three times with perfect timing.
"Come in," said a voice from inside.
It was feminine but had an edge that made it sound like it was used to being obeyed.
Helena glanced at them to signal a warning. "Be respectful, okay? Her mood is unpredictable," she said before opening the doors and ushering them inside.

Rex thought the office was just what someone with a lot of power would have. The space was big but not showy, with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves on two walls, a huge desk positioned to take advantage of the windows that offered a panoramic view of the city, and comfortable seating arranged so that people could talk without breaking the space’s implicit hierarchy.
Valentina Von Starlight stood up from her chair behind the desk with fluid grace.
Rex felt his assessment protocols kick in on their own, recording information with the kind of clinical accuracy that his old life had taught him and his new skills had improved.
’Holy fucking shit... there’s no fucking way, right...? She’s a grandmother, with that kind of peak body—even more peak than Helena...!?’
To put it bluntly, she wasn’t what he had expected when Helena talked about her mother.

Valentina’s hair was not the dull gray of old, but it was a shiny platinum that caught the light and seemed to glow with it. It was styled in a complicated way that made it look both formal and useful.
It was held in place by what looked like decorative pins that were probably also magical focuses.
But everything else about her was so different from a grandmother that Rex had to keep reminding himself that this woman had a daughter in her forties and grandchildren in their twenties.
"Just by seeing her... I feel an overwhelming desire to claim her as my own before I proceed with my mission!" The moment he thought that, he felt a rush of arousal that awakened his boner.
’Ah, crap! Thank the lust I wore baggy pants to hide my goddamn boner.’

Rex observed that her face possessed a refined beauty, a result of her good genes, self-care, and possibly a touch of magic. There were lines at the corners of her eyes and mouth, but they made her look wiser and more experienced, and not older with wrinkles.
Her skin was smooth and pale, and she had the kind of perfect complexion that usually only comes with youth or a lot of ’bullshit’ magic.

And her body, which was easy to see even though she was wearing formal robes that were both professional and subtly form-fitting, was in perfect shape. Rex could see the definition of toned muscle through the fabric.
This body type came from years of combat training and magical practice, and it was kept up through discipline and probably enhanced by carefully applied enhancement magic.
And what’s even better is that her breasts, ass, and even hips are even bigger and mellower than Helena’s.
If Rex was being honest with himself, she looked like someone in their late twenties or early thirties who had decided to dye their hair white for looks.
[VALENTINA VON STARLIGHT DETECTED]
[AGE: 68 - CLASSIFICATION: MAGE/ADMINISTRATOR]
[SYSTEM NOTE: NOT A REINCARNATOR, NATIVE HIGH-LEVEL PRACTITIONER]
[POWER LEVEL: EXTREME - DO NOT ANTAGONIZE]
[DESIRE LEVEL: 0/100]
[STATUS: ELIGIBLE TARGET - PROCEED WITH CAUTION]
’And, of course, she’s going to be a hard one for me to conquer...’
’...but still, who could stop me?’

chapters.title: Chapter 90. I Was Busy Admiring the GILF Valentina, and Then Helena Just Sold Me Out
paragraphs: Rex held back his reaction to the system notification and tried to keep the right look of respectful interest on his face, even though right now, his mind was full of fucked-up things he could do to Valentina.
Furthermore, his foresight succeeded in identifying any potentially dangerous mind-reading or telepathy abilities in Valentina, and there’s none. If she has one, Rex knows he fucked up.

Valentina looked around the group, and there was nothing warm or grandmotherly about her look. It was the judgment of someone who was excellent at judging threats, assets, and everything else with ruthless efficiency.
When her eyes met Rex’s, he felt like she was really looking at him, like she was seeing a lot more than he was comfortable with.
’That look... a rather strong woman indeed, and it’s going to be even better if I can break that vision of hers.’
Then she lost interest, and her face softened a little as she looked at her grandchildren.
"Elliot... Diana... Lily..." Her voice was calm and formal, but there was a hint of real love behind the professional distance. "I’m glad to see you all made it back safely."
"Grandmother," Elliot said, moving forward to bow in a respectful way.
She nodded in response.

Diana and Lily both came over, and Valentina smiled a little when Lily broke the rules and hugged her directly. Valentina’s hand came up to stroke Lily’s hair in a way that showed this was their special relationship.
The hug was surprisingly warm.
"Oh my, Lily... You’ve grown so much." Valentina said softly, "But... I see you’re still as recklessly loving as ever."
"Hehehe~! I can’t help it when I miss you, Grandma!" Lily said as she pulled back but stayed close.
"I miss you too," Valentina said as she looked at Helena. "Daughter... your report?"
Helena stood up straight, and just like that, the family dynamic changed back to something more formal. "The Goblin King incident was handled well, with a few deaths of innocent civilians."
"The bandit raid caused some damage to the village but no deaths, and the demon attack on the road here was stopped without any losses."
"The civilian refugees have been moved safely and are now being processed to become one with Aethelgard."
Valentina nodded slowly, and it was clear that she was processing the information quickly. "And the person who helped win these battles?"
She looked at Rex again. "I guess this is the man who’s called Rex Rexilion?"
"Yes, Mother," Helena said. "He’s a reincarnator who came to the village about two weeks ago."

Rex was shocked to his bones when hearing Helena spill that out of the blue, and it almost gave him a heart attack. It’s because he was so focused on admiring Valentina that his foresight went off for a second.
’What the fuck...!? W-Why did she just snitch on me like that...!?’
’That fucking bitch...! Even with that high-level desire, she still cannot be trusted until I break her.’
And now that the truth has been spilled free, he didn’t have any choice but to admit it. But at least some reincarnators are valued.

"He’s one of those reincarnators that’s worthy to be living in this world because of how he has been very helpful in many fights and has saved lives more than once, including Elliot’s during the Goblin King fight."

Rex felt like everyone in the room was looking at him, especially Evelyn, who looked even more shocked knowing that there’s a reincarnator close by after all this time. He kept his face neutral and respectful, letting Valentina set the pace of the conversation.

She looked at him for a long time, and Rex got the strong impression that she was seeing a lot more than just how he looked. He couldn’t tell if it was magical perception, a lot of experience reading people, or a mix of the two.
"Helena has written to me about what you’ve done," Valentina said at last. "Stepping in front of what should have been a fatal blow to protect my grandson."
"And fighting with my family against impossible odds... showing both bravery and skill in situations that would break other people."
"Now that’s a positive quality of a reincarnator. I respected his decision to live his second life here, just like other reincarnators out there who used their second chance for something useful."
She stopped for a moment, and something that looked like approval crossed her face. "Such service deserves praise and fair pay."
"Uh, well." Rex tilted his head. "I did what anyone else would have done."
"No." Valentina said, "Most people would have run away or frozen."
"You acted quickly and put yourself in danger for people you hardly knew, and it’s enough to show the character of who you are, which is much more important than power."
She walked around her desk and went right up to Rex. He could see that her eyes were a deep violet, which was unusual and striking.
They had the kind of penetrating intelligence that made him very aware that underestimating her would be a deadly mistake.
Valentina went on, "As for my gratitude for helping my family, I am giving you full enrollment as an honorable student in the Grand Academy of Magical Arts and Combat, effective immediately."
"You will have access to all facilities, instruction from our best professors, and the tools you need to reach your full potential."
Rex was really surprised hearing that. That was a lot more than he had thought, and it was very important from a strategic perspective.
Just by getting into the Academy meant getting knowledge, training, and most importantly, being close to the concentration of reincarnators and possible targets he had seen before.
"I’m honored," Rex said, his voice full of sincerity because he was thrilled about this. "And with all my respect... I’ll accept with my respectful gratitude."
It was clear that Helena was thrilled seeing how respectful Rex is. "Isn’t that great, Rex?!"
"You’ll be able to learn real magical theory, improve your fighting skills, and maybe even learn to stop relying on luck so much."
She said the last part with a teasing smile, and Rex easily smiled back. If only she knew how little luck had to do with his successes.
Valentina said, "There is, however, a condition," and her voice became more serious. "You must attend the Apostles meeting I called for this weekend."
Rex kept his face carefully blank, even though his system immediately sent out alert protocols. "Apostles...?"
"Apostles are something that can be identified when a mortal is blessed by the gods," Valentina said. "Reincarnators and natives alike who have the favor of the gods and fight for their gods."
"The capital has been gathering them in preparation for what’s coming."

She went back to her desk and pointed to a map that was spread out on it and had different symbols and notes on it. "Mordecai Vrael, the demon lord you’ve already known in passing, is not working alone.
"He’s part of a larger network of infernal nobility that’s been infiltrating the mortal realm for the past two years..."
"The Demon Seed vials, the planned attacks on settlements and trade routes, and the assassination attempts on important people—all of it is part of a plan to destabilize the region."
She pointed to a few places on the map that were marked. "We’ve found at least four major demon strongholds within a hundred miles of Aethelgard."
"Each one is making and spreading the Demon Seed, corrupting the people there, and building armies of transformed berserkers."
"The capital’s defenses are strong, but not unbreakable. We need people who can work together at the highest level to take action."
Elliot leaned forward, and his face was serious. "That’s why you called the Apostles."
"Exactly." Valentina looked at all of them. "The gods have their own reasons for keeping demons out."
"Each Apostle has special powers given to them by their patron deity. If we work together, we have a much better chance of destroying the demon strongholds before they can launch a major attack."

Rex quickly understood this information. So, the "Apostle gathering" was a formal event put together by someone with Valentina’s power to get divine champions to work together against a demonic threat.
That made sense of why Theo and the demons talked about it so casually. It seems that some people knew about it, and it’s not a secret anymore.
What’s more secret-worthy is his true colors, and he really needs to protect that with all his life.

He wanted to ask that so badly, but it could lead to something horrible, so he just stayed silent about it and asked Helena later when he got the chance while also talking about his reincarnator identity that got spilled without his permission.
Diana asked, "How many apostles are there that have answered?"
"Fourteen confirmed so far," Valentina said. "Along with Theo, who is a Paladin-rank Shielder for the Goddess of Life."
"I expect six more to show up before the week is over, bringing our total to about twenty."
Twenty apostles. There were twenty champions of different gods all in one place.
For someone like Rex, that was either the best chance they could have or the worst situation they could be in. Most likely both at the same time.
"I understand," Rex said carefully. "I’ll be there and help in any way I can."
Valentina looked at him for a little longer before nodding. "Good..."
"Helena will provide you with the details, and the gathering will take place in three days, giving you ample time to adjust to the Academy."
She focused on the whole group again. "You’re all free to go."
"Helena, I need to talk to you about some administrative issues for a few minutes."
"The rest of you can do whatever you want in the city or take a break."

Furthermore, his foresight succeeded in identifying any potentially dangerous mind-reading or telepathy abilities in Valentina, and there’s none.
If she has one, Rex knows he fucked up.
Valentina looked around the group, and there was nothing warm or grandmotherly about her look.
It was the judgment of someone who was excellent at judging threats, assets, and everything else with ruthless efficiency.
When her eyes met Rex’s, he felt like she was really looking at him, like she was seeing a lot more than he was comfortable with.
’That look... a rather strong woman indeed, and it’s going to be even better if I can break that vision of hers.’
Then she lost interest, and her face softened a little as she looked at her grandchildren.
"Elliot...
Diana...
Lily..." Her voice was calm and formal, but there was a hint of real love behind the professional distance.
"I’m glad to see you all made it back safely."
"Grandmother," Elliot said, moving forward to bow in a respectful way.
She nodded in response.
Diana and Lily both came over, and Valentina smiled a little when Lily broke the rules and hugged her directly.
Valentina’s hand came up to stroke Lily’s hair in a way that showed this was their special relationship.
The hug was surprisingly warm.
"Oh my, Lily...
You’ve grown so much." Valentina said softly, "But...
I see you’re still as recklessly loving as ever."
"Hehehe~!
I can’t help it when I miss you, Grandma!" Lily said as she pulled back but stayed close.
"I miss you too," Valentina said as she looked at Helena.
"Daughter... your report?"
Helena stood up straight, and just like that, the family dynamic changed back to something more formal.
"The Goblin King incident was handled well, with a few deaths of innocent civilians."
"The bandit raid caused some damage to the village but no deaths, and the demon attack on the road here was stopped without any losses."
"The civilian refugees have been moved safely and are now being processed to become one with Aethelgard."
Valentina nodded slowly, and it was clear that she was processing the information quickly.
"And the person who helped win these battles?"
She looked at Rex again.
"I guess this is the man who’s called Rex Rexilion?"
"Yes, Mother," Helena said.
"He’s a reincarnator who came to the village about two weeks ago."
Rex was shocked to his bones when hearing Helena spill that out of the blue, and it almost gave him a heart attack.
It’s because he was so focused on admiring Valentina that his foresight went off for a second.
’What the fuck...!?
W-Why did she just snitch on me like that...!?’
’That fucking bitch...!
Even with that high-level desire, she still cannot be trusted until I break her.’
And now that the truth has been spilled free, he didn’t have any choice but to admit it.
But at least some reincarnators are valued.

"He’s one of those reincarnators that’s worthy to be living in this world because of how he has been very helpful in many fights and has saved lives more than once, including Elliot’s during the Goblin King fight."
Rex felt like everyone in the room was looking at him, especially Evelyn, who looked even more shocked knowing that there’s a reincarnator close by after all this time.
He kept his face neutral and respectful, letting Valentina set the pace of the conversation.
She looked at him for a long time, and Rex got the strong impression that she was seeing a lot more than just how he looked.
He couldn’t tell if it was magical perception, a lot of experience reading people, or a mix of the two.
"Helena has written to me about what you’ve done," Valentina said at last.
"Stepping in front of what should have been a fatal blow to protect my grandson."
"And fighting with my family against impossible odds... showing both bravery and skill in situations that would break other people."
"Now that’s a positive quality of a reincarnator.
I respected his decision to live his second life here, just like other reincarnators out there who used their second chance for something useful."
She stopped for a moment, and something that looked like approval crossed her face.
"Such service deserves praise and fair pay."
"Uh, well." Rex tilted his head.
"I did what anyone else would have done."
"No." Valentina said, "Most people would have run away or frozen."
"You acted quickly and put yourself in danger for people you hardly knew, and it’s enough to show the character of who you are, which is much more important than power."
She walked around her desk and went right up to Rex.
He could see that her eyes were a deep violet, which was unusual and striking.
They had the kind of penetrating intelligence that made him very aware that underestimating her would be a deadly mistake.
Valentina went on, "As for my gratitude for helping my family, I am giving you full enrollment as an honorable student in the Grand Academy of Magical Arts and Combat, effective immediately."
"You will have access to all facilities, instruction from our best professors, and the tools you need to reach your full potential."
Rex was really surprised hearing that.
That was a lot more than he had thought, and it was very important from a strategic perspective.
Just by getting into the Academy meant getting knowledge, training, and most importantly, being close to the concentration of reincarnators and possible targets he had seen before.
"I’m honored," Rex said, his voice full of sincerity because he was thrilled about this.
"And with all my respect...
I’ll accept with my respectful gratitude."
It was clear that Helena was thrilled seeing how respectful Rex is.
"Isn’t that great, Rex?!"
"You’ll be able to learn real magical theory, improve your fighting skills, and maybe even learn to stop relying on luck so much."
She said the last part with a teasing smile, and Rex easily smiled back.
If only she knew how little luck had to do with his successes.
Valentina said, "There is, however, a condition," and her voice became more serious.
"You must attend the Apostles meeting I called for this weekend."
Rex kept his face carefully blank, even though his system immediately sent out alert protocols.
"Apostles...?"
"Apostles are something that can be identified when a mortal is blessed by the gods," Valentina said.
"Reincarnators and natives alike who have the favor of the gods and fight for their gods."
"The capital has been gathering them in preparation for what’s coming."

"We’ve found at least four major demon strongholds within a hundred miles of Aethelgard."
"Each one is making and spreading the Demon Seed, corrupting the people there, and building armies of transformed berserkers."

We need people who can work together at the highest level to take action."
Elliot leaned forward, and his face was serious.

If we work together, we have a much better chance of destroying the demon strongholds before they can launch a major attack."

chapters.title: Chapter 91. The Nightwing Family Has Committed Crimes Against the Normal Rules of Aging
paragraphs: It was a clear dismissal, delivered with the kind of authority that made arguing unthinkable. Elliot, Diana, Lily, and Evelyn all offered respectful farewells and filed out.
Rex followed, casting one last glance back at Valentina, who had already turned to speak with Helena in low tones.
The door shut behind them, leaving Rex in the hallway alongside the younger Starlights.
Elliot said, "So," with a smile.
"Well, I guess this is your official welcome as a new student to the Academy, and what’s even cooler is that you’re already an honorable student."
"Grandmother doesn’t give gifts like that for free." Diana added, "She must really appreciate what you did for us."
Lily said, "I’m just happy you’ll be around more," and she put her arm through Rex’s, which was becoming a habit.
"Having you close by will be nice."
Rex smiled and let them take him back down the grand staircase. His mind was already racing with what all of this meant.
Three days until the Apostle meeting. Twenty heavenly champions in one place.

Apollo Brightsoul is likely one of the twenty heavenly champions. Additionally, Rex himself is secretly serving a goddess whom most of the other champions would likely view as an enemy if they were aware of it.
This was going to be fun.
When they left the academy, they saw Theo and Iris waiting for them in the plaza, along with a few women Rex didn’t know but who caught his eye for several reasons.
Rex thought to himself. ’Oh...? What’s this...? Another woman that I could take?’

The first thing that caught his eye was a woman who looked like she had been made to be a "fighter-type warrior." She was tall, almost six feet, and her body type suggested that she could break stone with her bare hands.
Her hair was jet black and long in a way that kept it out of her face. She wore a revealing leather vest that showed off her muscles and pants that were made for movement instead of modesty.
Upon seeing Diana, the woman’s face burst into joy, a sudden change in expression that defied her intimidating appearance. "Oh my~! Would you look at that!?"
"It’s my favorite girl for Theo, Diana Von Starlight!"

The warrior woman crossed the space between them in three long strides and hugged Diana so tightly that she couldn’t move. Diana made a muffled sound of protest that was cut off when her face was pressed right into the woman’s big breast.
Her feet kicked a little as she fought for air.
"Ngh... I..." Diana was able to wheeze out, "...can’t breathe."
"Oh! Sorry!" The woman let go of Diana’s hand just enough for her to gasp for air, but she didn’t let her go. "It’s so good to see you again, Diana~! How long has it been—Ah! It’s been months!"
"Aurelia," Iris said with a smile. "You’re going to kill her if you keep hugging her like that without having to realize your strength."
Aurelia Noctis Nightwing, who is Theo’s mother and Iris’ older sister, was identified by Rex’s system as a "high-level combatant" rather than a reincarnator.
She finally let Diana go, and she stumbled back, looking flushed and disheveled.
Diana said, "H-Hi... Miss Aurelia," as she fixed her clothes. "It’s nice to see you too.
"Oh please~! Stop with the formalities; you know you can call me Mommy now!" Aurelia giggled while winking at her.
Diana gasped. "M-Mommy!?"
Two other women stood behind Aurelia. Despite being significantly older than Aurelia, they shared certain features that indicated their relationship.
’More baddies are coming in...!? And perhaps... more GILFs just like the title said!?’

The first woman looked to be about Valentina’s age. She had long white hair that was styled in a complicated braid and wore formal robes that were cut in a way that made it clear she didn’t want to look modest or reserved.
She stood up straight and had a look on her face that showed she thought she was better than everyone else.
Morwanna Nightwing, the system noted. Great-grandmother to Theo and Iris. Age 72. Power level: Extreme.
’GREAT GRANDMOTHER!? WITH THAT FUCKING APPEARANCE!?’ Rex was shocked to see that her age was older than Valentina’s.
’I fucking love fantasy worlds... hail fantasy worlds with their unique logic!’
’If it’s back in my world... they probably can’t—yeah, pause, I don’t want to get cancelled here.’
And then, there’s the second woman, who was younger—well, not younger, probably in her fifties. Her hair was changing from black to white in a way that made her look more beautiful than old.
She wore glasses that made her look like a scholar, and her clothes were both stylish and useful. When she looked at Rex, her eyes showed clear interest that was both judging and grateful.
Elaris Morr Nightwing, the system provided. Grandmother to Theo and Iris, daughter to Morwanna. Age 53. Power level: High.
’Another one... holy shit... and the way she dressed really did awaken my secret weapon that’s about to be unleashed.’
Rex’s mind was torn between making a list of threats and realizing that the Nightwing family seemed to have genetics that went against the normal rules of aging.
"Mother, Grandmother," Iris said, moving to greet them with obvious love. "I didn’t know you were coming to see us."
"Like we’d miss the chance," Elaris said, and then she saw Rex, and her smile grew even bigger. "Oh my... who is this good-looking young man?"
She walked toward Rex with purpose and grace. Before he could say anything, she was right next to him, one hand on his chest and the other looking up at him through her glasses.
’I see now... a teasing GILF, huh? My fucking favorite...’
"My, oh my... Helena didn’t say she had such a nice travel partner."
"Mother," Aurelia said, reaching out to pull Elaris away by the shoulder. "Please be respectful of him. You’re making everyone in this family look bad."
"Jeez... I’m not embarrassing anyone," Elaris said, but she let herself be moved.
She smiled at Rex and bowed her head down. "Sorry about that... I forget how to act when I’m interested in something."
"Don’t worry about it," Rex said smoothly while also bowing down, putting away the fact that Elaris didn’t seem to have any limits and wasn’t ashamed to show interest.
That could have been helpful information, and he already knows she could be his next target to get that 1000 desire energy.
[ELARIS MORR NIGHTWING: 0/100 → 5/100]
[REASON: IMMEDIATE PHYSICAL ATTRACTION, NO FILTER]
’Now... that’s interesting. Five points for a single interaction based only on physical attraction... it seems like she’s going to be an effortless target.’
’I fucking love teasing women.’
"My name is Rex Rexilion," he said, bowing respectfully and giving a proper introduction. "It’s a pleasure to meet all of you."
"I’ve been traveling with the Starlight family for the past few weeks."
Morwanna said, "The honor is ours," and her voice had the kind of weight that made it clear she was used to being listened to.
"Anyone who fights with our extended family is worth knowing, but I’m curious about how good you are."
Her eyes seemed to see through him in a way that made him feel uneasy, and Rex had the strong feeling that she was judging him much more deeply than the others.
Rex said, "I do what I can."
"Hmph." Morwanna’s face didn’t change, but something in her eyes said she thought he was intriguing. "We’ll see."
Then she looked at Valentina, who had apparently finished talking to Helena and come out of the Academy. "Valentina, we need to talk about the wards in private."
"Understood," Valentina said, and the two older women walked away together.
Their conversation quickly turned into low tones that made it sound like they were talking about something important.
Rex was left with the rest of the group, which now included the Starlights and the Nightwing family members who were visible.

Theo was standing next to Diana in a way that made it look like he didn’t know how close he was, but Diana did. Evelyn and Elliot were talking to Iris about something having to do with guard rotations.
Lily had once more attached herself to Rex’s side. Aurelia was looking at all of them with a knowing smile that made it seem like she knew things about the people in the room that they didn’t.
"You know," Aurelia said in a casual tone, looking directly at Theo, "it’s really nice how close the Starlight and Nightwing families have become over the years."
"We’re almost family already."
Theo nodded without really thinking about it. "Lady Valentina and Grandma Morwanna have been friends for decades, so it makes sense that the rest of us would be too."
"Exactly!" Aurelia’s smile got bigger. "That’s why I keep thinking it would be nice if we made it official, like through marriage or something like that."
Theo blinked, which showed that he didn’t get it. "Marriage...? Who is getting married?"
Rex thought to himself. ’My god... this fucking troupe of dense characters is killing me! What a fucking loser!’
Diana’s face was bright red, and she was carefully looking at the cobblestones.
Iris was trying not to laugh.
Lily was smiling like this was the best thing she’d seen in weeks.
Aurelia said in a very serious tone, "Well, there are many eligible bachelors and bachelorettes between our families..."
"It would be a shame if none of them found good partners, don’t you think?"
She looked Theo in the eye. "For example, you’re what, twenty-six now?"
"You’re definitely old enough to start thinking about settling down... and Diana here is twenty-six too."
"She’s accomplished, beautiful, and comes from a great family..."

chapters.title: Chapter 92. Helena Paid for My Room. I Will Use This Time Wisely and She Won’t Like How.
paragraphs: "Nargh?!" Diana made a noise that could have been a strangled protest.
Theo’s face changed from mild confusion to dawning realization that he was being set up. "M-Mother, I don’t think—"
Aurelia pushed, "You don’t think Diana would be a great match?" Her voice was innocent, but her eyes sparkled with mischief.
"Oh no... you broke your mother’s heart by saying that, but...! I think she’s great."
"N-No, of course I didn’t say she’s not a great match, b-but yeah...! I think she’s great too," Theo said quickly, but then he seemed to remember what he had said and tried to take it back.
"N-Not that I’ve been thinking about it that way, I just meant that she’s a very capable person and—"
"Objectively capable," Iris said again, this time not even trying to hide her laughter. "How sweet."
Diana had apparently decided that the ground was fascinating and didn’t want to look at anyone, and she was also trying so hard not to scream loudly or die right now because of embarrassment.
Lily was almost shaking with laughter that she was holding back.

Rex found the whole conversation very interesting and stored away all the information he could about how things were going. Theo was genuinely unaware of what was happening; however, he already knew he was a dim-witted, incompetent individual.
And he can clearly tell Diana was embarrassed, but she was also clearly interested. Aurelia was having a great time teasing both of them.
’It’s either Diana or Elaris... but at least both of them are connected to that loser, so it’s still a win-win situation for me’
And everyone else was having a good time with the show.

Elaris interrupted, feeling sorry for Theo, and said, "I think what my dear daughter is trying to say is that it would be nice if the younger generation spent more time together getting to know each other and making connections."
She stressed the word "connections" in a way that made it very clear she was talking about romantic relationships. Theo finally seemed to get that she was really teasing him.
He said, "I will certainly keep that in mind," in a way that was so neutral that it seemed like he was trying to get out of the conversation as quickly as possible.
"D-Diana, maybe we could train together this week? I’d like to see how you’ve improved your archery skills."
Diana finally looked up, and her face was carefully blank. "I... I’d like that."
"Great," Theo said, taking advantage of the chance. "Iris, we should probably check on the housing assignments for the refugees."
"Rex, maybe I have to say this again with full respect..." Theo held his chest. "It was nice meeting you, so I’m sure we’ll have more time to talk later on."
Rex nodded. "Likewise.
He practically fled, and Iris followed, though not before shooting Diana a look that was pure mischief.
"That went well," Aurelia said cheerfully after they left.
Diana said, "You’re terrible as always, Miss Aurelia," but there wasn’t much anger in it.
"I like ’lovingly direct’ better." Aurelia said, "Plus, that boy needs a push, or he’ll be sixty before he gets it."
Rex saved the whole conversation as useful information. The family dynamics were complicated, the teasing was good-natured, and it seemed clear to everyone but Theo that Diana liked him.
This information is useful for future reference, and he can leverage that psychological dominance over Theo after increasing Diana’s desire level to 100.
’For now... I need to adapt to the capital first so that I can see more clearly future plans.’
The next few hours flew by as we met people and went on tours. Helena insisted on giving them a proper tour of Aethelgard, pointing out important places and neighborhoods.
The crafting quarter was where magical items were made and enchanted. The merchant district is home to large markets that offer a wide range of products, from everyday necessities to unique imports.
The residential areas encompassed a wide range of housing options, from modest apartments to luxurious estates. The various government buildings were integral to the functioning of the city.
Rex took it all in, making a mental map of where things were, writing down security measures, and generally getting ready for the next few weeks.
They had seen most of the city by the time the afternoon turned into evening. Helena finally took them to what she called "one last stop before we settle everyone in for the night."
The inn they were going to was huge, at least three times the size of the Broken Wheel in the village. It took up the whole corner block in what looked like a wealthy area near the business center.
A sign that said "The Silver Rest" hung over an entrance that could fit several groups at once.
Helena said, "This is where Marceline works," as they walked in.
"We studied together at the Academy years ago, but she chose to run a business instead of practicing combat magic."
The inside was cozy and welcoming, with a big common room with tables and a bar that ran along one wall. The place was busy but not too crowded.
People were eating, drinking, and talking, which made it clear that they were regulars.
There was a woman behind the bar who looked about Helena’s age. She had short light brown hair pulled back in a practical way and an apron that made it look like she had been working in the kitchen.
When they came in, she looked up and smiled with real joy when she saw Helena.

"Helena! My goodness~! It’s good to see you made it back safely!" She quickly came around the bar and wiped her hands on her apron. "I’ve been listening for you since your letter said to expect you today or tomorrow."
Helena said, "Marceline, it’s good to see you," and they hugged for a moment like old friends.
"Let me introduce you all."
She gestured to Mara and Garrett, who had been silent all day but were now surveying the inn. "This is Mara and Garrett Kesson."
"I wrote about them in my letter because they used to own the Broken Wheel Inn, but it was damaged in a bandit raid. You got it, right?"

"Of course!" Marceline’s smile was warm and real, and she turned her attention to them right away. "Helena wrote that you were experienced innkeepers looking for temporary work while you got established in the capital."
"I can’t tell you how perfect the timing is. We’ve been so busy lately with all the traffic from the Apostle gathering preparations, and I’ve been in desperate need of reliable help."
"We’d be happy to help," Garrett said, and Mara nodded in agreement, looking relieved.
"Wonderful!" Marceline said as she put her hands together. "You’ll get a place to live and eat, as well as regular pay for your work."
"If you’re not too tired, I can show you everything tonight, or we can wait until morning and start over."
"Tonight works," Mara said, looking at Garrett to make sure. "We’d like to get started."
"Perfect." Marceline turned her attention to Rex. "And who is this young man?"
"Rex Rexilion," Helena said. "He’s been helping Mara and Garrett with work and odd jobs."
Rex looked at Marceline, and yet again he was pleased to see many women that he could take. ’She really reminds me of Mara, but she looks more motherly... what I fucking love the most, of course.’
"I was hoping you could find room for him, too, but I’d like to pay for his stay directly as payment for the work he did while we were traveling."
Rex began to complain because that seemed too much, but Helena stopped him with a look.
"You saved my son’s life." She said, "You helped keep my family safe through many dangers."
"The least I can do is make sure you have a safe place to stay while you get settled here. That’s all there is to it."

Marceline looked back and forth between them, clearly sensing that there was more to the story but not wanting to get involved. "I have a few rooms on the third floor that are quiet, private, and away from the noise of the main common room."
"They’re perfect for someone who needs a place to study or train."
Helena asked, "So how much for... umm... three months?"

chapters.title: Chapter 93. Apollo Brightsoul Has No Idea What’s Coming. Neither Does Anyone Else.
paragraphs: Marceline gave Rex a price that he thought was below market value, probably as a favor to Helena. Helena paid right away, counting out coins like someone who didn’t care much about money but found it useful.
She turned to Rex and said, "There we go."
"You’re paid through the end of the season."
"Marceline here will take care of anything you need, and I’ll be staying with Mother at her estate on the Academy grounds, but you can reach me there if you need something."
"Thank you, Helena," Rex said, and he meant it. "This is very kind of you, and I don’t know much of how to repay that kind of stuff."
"Oh, come on now, Rex. Don’t act like a stranger with that talk," Helena said, but her face was warm. "You’ll be going to the Academy, so you’ll need a place to sleep and study nearby."
"This is the perfect place, and I’ll let Lily hang once in a while." Helena giggled with a teasing look.
That look immediately shot Rex in the heart because he knew that Helena probably realized what had happened to her daughter Lily, who was always attached to him.
She said her goodbyes, then she picked up Elliot, Diana, Lily, and Evelyn with the clear goal of getting them settled at the Starlight estate.
Before she left, Lily hugged Rex tightly and whispered, "See you tomorrow," in a way that made it clear she was already thinking about when they would be alone again.
"Yeah, this is why Helena looks like this. It could also be my way to get close to Valentina and the Nightwing family."
In the common room, only Rex, Mara, Garrett, and Marceline were left.
"I’ll show you to your rooms." Marceline said, "We can do the whole tour later, but at least you know where you’re going to sleep."

She showed them around the inn, pointing out the kitchen, storage areas, and staff rooms along the way. Mara and Garrett got a small but comfortable room on the second floor, not far from where they would be helping to run things.
They took Rex up to the third floor and into a room at the end of a quiet hallway.
Marceline opened the door and jokingly said, "And here we have your own mini castle to live in."

Rex had thought the room would be smaller, but it was actually bigger. It had a real king-size bed instead of a cot, a desk by the window for light, a wardrobe for storage, and even a small seating area with two chairs.
The furniture was simple but well-made, and it was meant to be comfortable for a long time, not just for a short stay.
’A king-size fucking bed... now this shit is good! If only there were a camera in this world, I could make a lot of porn videos with all the women I steal.’
Marcelina said, "Just let me know if you need anything, like extra blankets, meals outside of regular dining hours, or information about the capital."
"During business hours, I’m usually in the common room or the kitchen. If you need something right away, my personal quarters are on the second floor."
"Thank you so much." Rex said, "This is just right."

Rex saw that Marceline’s smile changed her face from just lovely to really beautiful. She was in her late thirties and had the kind of mature beauty that made it look like she had aged well and would keep doing so.
Her eyes were kind but smart, and she had a natural warmth about her that made her seem like she was just doing her job.
[MARCELINE BANCEY DETECTED]
[AGE: 38 - CLASSIFICATION: INNKEEPER/CIVILIAN]
[STATUS: NOT A REINCARNATOR]
[DESIRE LEVEL: 0/100]
[STATUS: ELIGIBLE TARGET]
Rex put her in a file as someone he wanted to get to know better. She was lovely, well-known in the area, and had already shown that she was kind.
All of these traits made her a desirable target for future attention.
"Alright then, I’ll let you get settled for now." Marceline said, "Oh, and... Rex, welcome to the Silver Rest."
"I hope you feel at home here."
She left and shut the door behind her, and then Rex was finally alone.

He went to the window first and looked out over the capital as night fell. Aethelgard stretched out in front of him, lit by thousands of magical lights that made a tapestry of light against the darkening sky.
From this perspective, he could see the Academy’s towers rising above everything else. Beyond them, he could see the huge walls that kept the capital safe from outside threats.
Then he went to the bed and lay down, feeling how real the mattress was and being grateful that he had somehow ended up in such a comfortable situation.
And it’s time to find out some important information for him in the future.
"System," he said softly, knowing that the words would only be in his head. "I need to understand something better."
"The demons talked about a ’Apostle gathering.’ Valentina said it’s a formal event where divine champions work together to fight threats."
"But... the thing is, how well-known is this idea of Apostles? Why did Theo and others talk about it so casually?"
[INFORMATION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGED]
[ACCESSING RELEVANT DATA]
[APOSTLES: WIDELY RECOGNIZED PHENOMENON IN THIS WORLD]
[EXPLANATION: DIVINE INTERVENTION THROUGH MORTAL CHAMPIONS IS ESTABLISHED HISTORICAL FACT, NOT SECRET KNOWLEDGE]
[CURRENT ERA: APPROXIMATELY 200-300 ACTIVE APOSTLES ACROSS THE KNOWN WORLD]
[DISTRIBUTION: VARIOUS GODS AND GODDESSES MAINTAIN CHAMPIONS FOR THEIR INTERESTS]
[PUBLIC KNOWLEDGE: MOST EDUCATED INDIVIDUALS AWARE OF APOSTLE EXISTENCE AND GENERAL FUNCTION]
[GATHERINGS: OCCUR OCCASIONALLY WHEN MAJOR THREATS REQUIRE COORDINATED DIVINE CHAMPION RESPONSE]
[CURRENT GATHERING: ORGANIZED BY VALENTINA VON STARLIGHT IN RESPONSE TO MORDECAI VRAEL’S DEMON LORD ACTIVITIES]
[EXPECTED ATTENDANCE: 20-25 APOSTLES OF VARIOUS RANKS AND DIVINE PATRONS]
[YOUR STATUS: SECRET - ONLY YOU AND LUSTIA AWARE OF YOUR APOSTLE OF LUST DESIGNATION]
[RECOMMENDATION: MAINTAIN COVER AS ORDINARY REINCARNATOR UNTIL STRATEGIC ADVANTAGE REQUIRES REVELATION]
Rex thought carefully about that information. People like Theo and the demons could talk about Apostles without thinking too much about it.
The idea wasn’t secret or strange; it was just a well-known group of people with power and trust from the gods or goddesses.
So, when Rex finally showed his Lustful Villain form, he wouldn’t have to explain what an Apostle was. People would already know what the basic idea was.
They wouldn’t know which god had blessed him or even who he was because of his secret identity, and that was something he could control when he told them.
Rex asked, "How many Apostles of Life are there compared to other types?"
[APOSTLES OF LIFE: APPROXIMATELY 40-50 ACTIVE]
[APOSTLES OF OTHER MAJOR GODS: 30-40 EACH]
[APOSTLES OF FORBIDDEN GODS (INCLUDING YOURSELF): ESTIMATED 20-30 TOTAL, MOSTLY OPERATING IN SECRET]
[NOTE: GODDESS OF LIFE MOST ACTIVE IN APOSTLE CREATION DUE TO HER EMPHASIS ON HEROISM AND SAVING MORTALS]
[NOTE: FORBIDDEN GOD APOSTLES RARELY ADVERTISE THEIR PATRON TO AVOID PERSECUTION]
And that was exactly what Lustia had told him. The Goddess of Life was very pushy about giving champions power, which meant that Rex would have many targets to find and kill.
But the Forbidden God Apostles kept their ties secret, so Rex could be the Lustful Villain without anyone knowing right away that he was working for Lustia.
"Last question." Rex said, "The Apostle gathering is in three days. What’s the plan? How does it work?"
[APOSTLE GATHERINGS: TYPICALLY FORMAL COORDINATION MEETINGS]
[STRUCTURE: HOSTED BY LOCAL AUTHORITY (IN THIS CASE, VALENTINA VON STARLIGHT)]
[PURPOSE: SHARE INTELLIGENCE, COORDINATE STRATEGIES, ASSIGN ROLES FOR UPCOMING OPERATIONS]
[ATTENDANCE: VOLUNTARY BUT STRONGLY ENCOURAGED FOR REGIONAL APOSTLES]
[EXPECTED OUTCOME: FORMATION OF STRIKE TEAMS TO TARGET DEMON STRONGHOLDS]
[YOUR ROLE: ATTEND AS NEWLY RECOGNIZED REINCARNATOR, OBSERVE AND GATHER INTELLIGENCE ON OTHER APOSTLES]
[OPPORTUNITY: IDENTIFY PRIORITY TARGETS FOR FUTURE ELIMINATION, ESTABLISH CONTACTS AND ALLIANCES]
In the dark, Rex smiled.
He needs exactly three days to get ready.
He needs three days to adjust to the Academy, familiarize himself with the students, and strategize how to manage the gathering.
Three days from now, he would find himself in the same room as Apollo Brightsoul and possibly a dozen other Apostles of Life.
The mark on his hand pulsed once, barely noticeable, as if it was responding to his excitement.
"This shit is going to be very interesting..."
